papers.title: Revisiting the $\beta_1$-action on the 3-primary stable homotopy groups of spheres
papers.abstract: Let $\beta_1$ be the first 3-torsion class in the stable homotopy groups of spheres in even degree. Toda showed that $\beta_1^5 \neq 0$, whilst $\beta_1^6 = 0$. Shimomura generalised this to the 144-periodic family generated by $\beta_1$, written as $\{\beta_{1+9s}\}_{s\geq 0}$, and showed that any $5$-fold product $\prod_5 \beta_{1+9s} \neq 0$, whilst all 6-fold products $\prod_6 \beta_{1+9s} = 0$. In this article, we give a simple proof of these results as well as some generalisations to other 144-periodic families. Along the way, we also refine known detection results for these families. Our tools include BP-synthetic spectra, and the well-known Adams--Novikov spectral sequence for the spectrum of topological modular forms at the prime $3$ as well as its Adams operations.

papers.title: An $(\infty,1)$-category of conically smooth stratified bordisms
papers.abstract:
To study derived defect topological quantum field theories, we construct an $(\infty,1)$-category of stratified bordisms and sketch its $(\infty,d)$-dimensional analogue.
  In the first chapters we develop a method for constructing symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories, inspired by Segal spaces but better suited to geometric inputs, which we call interval Segal spaces. Using this framework, we construct the $(\infty,1)$-category of $d$-dimensional smooth manifolds via smooth $\infty$-sheaves thereof, in an attempt to address fibrancy issues present in prior work on this subject. We further equip this category with a symmetric monoidal structure, compute its homotopy 1-category, and extend the construction to manifolds endowed with tangential structures, obtaining the interval Segal space of $d$-dimensional bordisms with tangential structure.
  To model the stratifications supporting topological defects, we work with conically smooth stratified spaces, a suitably smooth framework for conical stratifications.
  We define stratified topological manifolds as stratified $\mathcal{B}$-manifolds for a suitable $(\infty,1)$-category of basics $\mathcal{B}$. Using these, we construct an interval Segal space whose objects are compact closed stratified topological $(d-1)$-manifolds and whose 1-morphisms are stratified $d$-dimensional bordisms, and we endow it with a symmetric monoidal structure. We also use tangential structures on conically smooth stratified spaces to formulate a notion of defect labels, aiming toward bordisms with labeled defects in the style of Carqueville et al.
  Finally, we sketch a higher-dimensional generalization of the interval category to a category of $d$-cubes for $d>1$, conjecturally presenting $(\infty,d)$-categories, and outline how stratified factorization homology may be used to produce derived stratified defect TQFTs.

papers.title: Cohesive 2-Topoi: Foundational Aspects and Nonabelian Differential Cohomology
papers.abstract: We provide a self-contained exposition of cohesive $(2,1)$-topos theory, its internal synthetic geometry, and its realization of intrinsic, modal, and differential nonabelian cohomology. Starting from the $(2,1)$-categorical hierarchy, Grothendieck $(2,1)$-topoi, effective internal groupoids, and $\E_k$-algebra objects over $(2,1)$-operads, we develop a detailed comparison between \emph{internal} and \emph{external} deloopings in $(2,1)$-presheaf and Grothendieck $(2,1)$-topoi. Specifically, we formalize external delooping by transporting the canonical delooping transformation along the group, discrete, and groupoid Yoneda 2-embeddings, proving that it is 2-naturally equivalent to the internal delooping in any Grothendieck $(2,1)$-topos. We then establish the 2-truncated Dunn--Lurie additivity, Baez--Dolan stabilization, and Eckmann--Hilton characterization of $k$-tuply groupal objects as groupal $\E_k$-algebras stabilizing at $k=3$, and clarify the truncation behavior of iterated deloopings $B_{\mathbf{H}}^k G$. Finally, we review Lawvere--Schreiber cohesive modalities, construct abstract principal $k$-bundles, the flat de Rham modality $\flat_{\dR}$, universal Maurer--Cartan forms $\theta_k$, connection moduli stacks $B^k_{\con}G$, and sharp-adjusted internal connection moduli $G\Conn^k(X)$. The paper culminates in synthetic differential cohomology, where we discuss extensions of the Maurer--Cartan morphism to non-groupal coefficients via $\int_{\dR} \dashv \flat_{\dR}$, and internal classifying structures.

papers.title: Equivariant intersection cohomology of some $4$-dimensional locally standard $T$-pseudomanifolds
papers.abstract: Locally standard $T$-pseudomanifolds are singular analogues of quasitoric manifolds. In this paper, we study a certain class of four-dimensional locally standard $T^2$-pseudomanifolds over convex polygons. We establish an Orlik-Raymond type classification and study their ordinary and equivariant cohomology, as well as their intersection and equivariant intersection cohomology. We also introduce ring structures on middle-perversity intersection cohomology and equivariant intersection cohomology via change of perversity. We show that these rings can be described in terms of the cohomology and equivariant cohomology of associated nonsingular spaces, which are quasitoric manifolds or $S^4$. Furthermore, we give combinatorial descriptions of the equivariant cohomology and equivariant intersection cohomology in terms of labelled graphs.

papers.title: Motivic Borel-Moore Homology is Borel-Moore Motivic Homology
papers.abstract: This paper studies the higher Chow groups of arbitrary finite type separated schemes using motivic homotopy theory, serving as a Borel-Moore counterpart to the $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant motivic cohomology of Bachmann-Elmanto-Morrow. We construct a filtration on the G-theory spectrum of a finite type separated scheme $X$, inducing an Atiyah-Hirzebruch style spectral sequence whose associated graded pieces are a complex computing the higher Chow groups of $X$. We prove that this complex is representable in the stable motivic homotopy category, and is a module over the $\mathbb{A}^1$-motivic complex, giving rise to an action of $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant motivic cohomology on the Bloch-Levine cycle complex. This generalizes some results of Bloch and Levine relating higher Chow groups and motivic cohomology to the case of schemes over an arbitrary base, and which need not be smooth or equidimensional.

papers.title: The $J$-Homomorphism From Localising The Cobordism Hypothesis
papers.abstract: Lurie's cobordism hypothesis classifies fully extended framed topological field theories valued in a symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-category $\mathcal{C}$ with duals by the $\infty$-groupoid $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{fd}}$ of fully dualisable objects. This classification results in an $O(n)$-action on $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{fd}}$, where $O(n)$ acts on the framed bordism category by change of framing. Lurie observed that for a connective spectrum, this action is ``a version of the classical $J$-homomorphism.'' We make this identification explicit: with respect to the right action of $O(n)$ on framings, the $O(n)$-action on the localisation $L(\mathrm{Bord}_n^{\mathrm{fr}}) \simeq S$ is precisely $\ominus J_n$, the inverse of the unstable $J$-homomorphism $J_n \colon O(n) \to \mathrm{GL}_1(S)$. The identification of the action with the unstable $J$-homomorphism in the setting of smooth stacks is due to Grady--Pavlov; we give an independent proof in Lurie's original formulation of the cobordism hypothesis, using the abstract Pontryagin--Thom construction. The sign (i.e.\ whether the action is $J_n$ or $\ominus J_n$) depends on the convention for the $O(n)$-action on framings, and is relevant for $\mathrm{pin}^\pm$ theories and hence for quantum systems with time-reversal symmetry. We compute the induced action on homotopy groups of the sphere spectrum in low degrees, yielding explicit invariants for invertible TFTs in dimensions $1$, $2$, and $3$, and connect these to the Kitaev chain, the framing anomaly, the spin-statistics theorem, and anomaly inflow. We recover the Galatius--Madsen--Tillmann--Weiss theorem as a consequence of the cobordism hypothesis and relate the homotopy fixed-point and mapping-spectrum perspectives on invertible TFTs via the duality between tangential and normal framings.

papers.title: A Note on the Cosupport of Balmer-Favi Idempotents
papers.abstract: Let $g_x$ be the Balmer-Favi idempotent at a point $x$ of the spectrum of a rigidly-compactly generated tensor triangulated category. We study the equality $\operatorname{Cosupp}(g_x)=\operatorname{gen}(x)$ by expressing $g_x$ as a local dual. We prove the equality for the derived category of a Noetherian scheme and for the stable module category of a finite group scheme over a field of positive characteristic. For $E(n)$-local spectra we express the maps between distinct monochromatic layers of the sphere in terms of the chromatic fracture square. The height-two splitting gives the equality through height two at every prime. For a Noetherian local ring we characterize the Gorenstein property by the form of its closed-point idempotent.

papers.title: A toric construction of the spectral Tate curve
papers.abstract: We develop toric geometry spectral algebraic geometry. In particular, we lift toric varieties to flat schemes over the sphere spectrum. Furthermore, we prove several rigidity and strictness results allowing us to define and produce strict group actions of flat algebraic tori. As an application, we give a construction of the Tate curve in spectral algebraic geometry. This approach lets us produce a lift of the Tate curve to $\mathbb{S}[[q]]$. We furthermore describe how to lift (arithmetic) toric stacks.

papers.title: Capacities from the Chiu-Tamarkin complex II: Product formula and toric domains
papers.abstract:
In this article, we continue our study of equivariant symplectic capacities of open sets in a cotangent bundle defined via the Chiu-Tamarkin complex constructed from the microlocal theory of sheaves.
  The paper consists of two parts: 1) We develop the theory of $S^1$-equivariant Chiu-Tamarkin complex over complex-oriented ring spectra. 2) Applications of the theory to symplectic capacities: We show that a product formula for the capacities, whose Ekeland-Hofer capacities version is folklore since 1988, is not true via an (uncountable family of) counterexample(s). The counterexample (family) is the product of a concave toric domain of dimension $6$ ($2n\geq 6$) and a $2$-dimensional disk. We also prove a Weyl law of the capacities for all toric domains in dimension $2n$. The algebraic verification is based on a chain model for the Chiu-Tamarkin complex of all toric domains in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, which recovers Irie's conjectural chain model of $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology for star-shaped toric domains (defined only) in $\mathbb{R}^4$.

papers.title: Klein four slices of the representation suspensions of $H\underline{\mathbb{F}_2}$
papers.abstract: We study the regular slice filtration of representation spheres $S^V\wedge H\underline{M}$. For every finite group $G$, we locate all slices in an explicit interval $[n(V),k(V)]$ and show that both endpoints occur. We introduce a \emph{defect vector} to measure a slice's failure. For the Klein four-group with $\underline{\mathbb F}_2$-coefficients, a balanced defect allows us to move $S^V\wedge H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ by certain $RO(G)$-graded cohomology classes to its $\dim V$-slice, which is again a representation sphere, while an odd defect obstructs any spherical slice. As an application, we obtain closed formulas for the bottom slice of $\Sigma^nH\underline{\mathbb{F}}_2$ for every $n$, recovering the computation of Guillou and Yarnall by a different method. Along the way, we determine the complete slice tower of $S^{\infty\alpha_i}\wedge H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ and consequently, the partial tower for $S^{n\alpha_i}\wedge H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$.

papers.title: M\"obius Invertibility of Rank Invariants
papers.abstract:
One of the best known invariants of multi-parameter persistent homology is the rank invariant, which is subsumed by the generalized rank invariant (GRI), obtained by naturally extending its domain. M\"obius inversion of the GRI not only provides a compact encoding of this invariant but is also useful for clarifying its relationship with other invariants of multi-parameter persistent homology. However, M\"obius inversion of the GRI has been defined only under suitable finiteness conditions on its domain and support. This work studies the extent to which M\"obius inversion can be extended beyond these finiteness conditions. Namely, we formalize the notion of M\"obius invertibility, which captures when M\"obius inversion exists beyond these finiteness conditions, and investigate when the GRI is M\"obius invertible.
  A central result we establish is that M\"obius invertibility of the GRI is guaranteed for finitely presentable $d$-parameter persistence modules when $d\leq 2$, but may fail when $d>2$. Establishing this failure also corrects an error in the existing literature. In response to this higher-dimensional obstruction, we show that for finitely presentable $d$-parameter persistence modules, restricting the GRI to intervals subordinate to the finite grid supporting a minimal free presentation preserves its M\"obius inversion whenever the latter exists over all intervals. Since computing the GRI over all intervals in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is infeasible in practice, this result provides a principled justification for restricting the GRI to those intervals.

papers.title: Quasi-F-split heights and derived Morita invariance
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study quasi-F-splitting from the viewpoint of non-commutative algebraic geometry. Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p. For a proper dg-category over k with a Serre functor, we define quasi-F^e-split heights for e\geq 1 by using finite topological restriction homology with coefficients in a shift of the Serre functor. Using the functoriality of polygonic topological Hochschild homology for laced categories due to Harpaz--Nikolaus--Saunier, we show that these heights are invariant under derived Morita equivalence. For a proper Gorenstein scheme of pure dimension over k, the height for e=1 of its dg-category of perfect complexes coincides with the quasi-F-split height in the sense of Yobuko. For a complete Noetherian Gorenstein local \(k\)-algebra with residue field k, the dg-category of perfect complexes supported at the closed point recovers the n-quasi-F^e-splitting of Tanaka--Witaszek--Yobuko for all n,e\geq 1. The proofs use the computation of the zeroth homotopy groups of TR with coefficients due to Dotto--Krause--Nikolaus--Patchkoria, Zariski descent, and Serre duality or local duality.

papers.title: Representability of Galois extensions
papers.abstract: We study faithful Galois extensions in a presentably symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category $\mathscr{C}$ by a dualizable $\mathbb{E}_1$-group $G$. We prove that these extensions correspond to colimit-preserving symmetric monoidal functors from $\mathrm{An}^{\mathrm{B}G}$ to $\mathscr{C}$. Under suitable assumptions, we use this correspondence to construct a Galois pro-anima that classifies Galois extensions in $\mathscr{C}$. This generalizes the \'etale fundamental groupoid of commutative rings and Mathew's weak Galois groupoid.

papers.title: The Dedekind-MacNeille Completion as a Functor
papers.abstract: We study the Dedekind-MacNeille completion through representable functors on the wide subcategory $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}$ of posets and lower cut-continuous (closed) maps. On this category the completion is contravariantly functorial and naturally isomorphic to $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}}(-,[1])^{\mathrm{op}}$, via $A\mapsto\chi_A$ and its inverse $f\mapsto f^{-1}(\{0\})$. The naturality of this identification makes the Yoneda lemma applicable: uniqueness of the representing object and the endomorphism monoid of the completion follow formally. We also show that $\mathbf{CLat}_\vee$ is full in $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}$, that $\mathbf{CLat}_\wedge$ is equivalent to a full subcategory of $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}^{\mathrm{op}}$, and that the covariant adjunction refines to a $2$-adjunction whose idempotent monad has Eilenberg--Moore algebras equivalent to $\mathbf{CLat}_\vee$.

papers.title: A notion of pseudo-morphisms with applications to the study of polynomial maps and of link-homotopy groups of 2-string link
papers.abstract: We introduce a notion of pseudo-morphism for groups, which extends the notion of group morphism from a group to a ring. We show that pseudo-morphisms from a group $G$ to an integral domain $R$ form a filtred Hopf algebra which can be seen as an efficient notion of dual for $G$. We also show that pseudo-morphisms are closely related to the notion of polynomial maps in the sense of Eilenberg-MacLane/Passi, the two notions even coinciding when $G$ is finitely generated and $R$ is a field. It follows that, in that case, polynomial maps are endowed with an Hopf structure. In a second part, we study non repeated Milnor invariants (in the $4$-dimensional context of $2$-string links) from this pseudo-morphism point of view. We show that they form a sub-bialgebra of the Hopf algebra of pseudo-morphisms on the group of $2$-string links up to link-homotopy, and prove that it is isomorphic to an explicit quotient $\textrm{Mil}$ of a polynomial ring. This leads to a fully algebraic description of the group of 2-string links up to link-homotopy as the dual group associated to $\textrm{Mil}$. As a by-product, we obtain that non repeated Milnor invariants are polynomial maps, and we show that this can be used to give a new proof of their finite type property.

papers.title: An Implementation of the 3-Dimensional Extended Persistent Homology Transform
papers.abstract: The Extended Persistent Homology Transform (XPHT) describes a shape through the extended persistence diagrams of its directional height functions. We present an algorithm for computing a finite directional sample of the three-dimensional XPHT from a triangulated boundary. Our main construction determines essential first-homology pairings by combining an ordered tree-cotree decomposition with evaluation-dual cocycles. The decomposition supplies a homology basis compatible with the height filtration, while the cocycles are used to determine the essential birth-death pairs. Degree-zero persistence and duality determine the remaining boundary diagrams. Under the boundary-reduction hypotheses and with critical-point sign labels, these diagrams yield the extended persistence of the solid. The resulting procedure uses graph constructions and linear algebra over F2 on boundary meshes extracted from three-dimensional binary images.

papers.title: Cyclic Hasse diagrams of manifolds and noncommutative path cohomology
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a connected oriented closed manifold of dimension $d\geq 2$, equipped with a regular CW structure, and let $P$ be its face poset. We consider the cyclic Hasse diagram $G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}}$, obtained from the directed Hasse diagram $G_P$ by adding an arrow from each maximal cell to every $0$-cell of $M$. Over an arbitrary field $\mathbb K$, we completely describe the path cohomology algebra $PH^*(G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}})$ in terms of the $\mathbb K$-Betti numbers of $M$. In particular, this algebra is not graded commutative whenever the dimension of $H^*(M)$ over $\mathbb K$ is at least 4. This disproves Grigor'yan's conjecture on graded commutativity. Moreover, as $M$ ranges over connected oriented closed surfaces, the even subalgebras $PH^{\mathrm{even}}(G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}})$, regarded as ungraded associative unital $\mathbb K$-algebras, satisfy no common algebraic identity beyond those satisfied by all associative unital $\mathbb K$-algebras. These results distinguish GLMY path cohomology from classical cohomology, whose cup product is graded commutative and whose even subalgebra is commutative. As an application, we construct a digraph $G$ for which the K\"unneth formula for the categorical product $G\times G$ fails, answering a question of Pinto negatively and disproving another conjecture of Grigor'yan.

papers.title: Cyclic homology of Sheaf Categories
papers.abstract: In this note, we explain the circle action on the Hochschild homology of categories of sheaves and their admissible subcategories in terms of the six-functor formalism using factorization homology, including (quasi-)coherent sheaves on derived stacks, sheaves on manifolds with prescribed microsupports, and Tamarkin categories with prescribed microsupports. We also explain the Gysin sequence for $C_\ell$ and $S^1$-(co)invariants and the K\"unneth sequence for $S^1$-(co)invariants of the Hochschild homology relative to any complex-oriented symmetric monoidal category.

papers.title: Finite generation of the second homology group of the genus three Torelli group
papers.abstract:
We prove that the group $H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely generated, where $\mathcal{I}_3$ is the Torelli subgroup of the mapping class group of a closed genus-three surface $\Sigma_3$. A key role in the proof is played by establishing the following property: for each symplectic transvection $t_x\in\mathrm{Sp}_{6}(\mathbb{Z})$, we have
  $$
  \bigl(t^{120}_x-1\bigr)^{57}\bigl(t_x^{24}-1\bigr)(t_x-1)^6H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})=0.
  $$
  The proof is based on the study of the spectral sequences associated with the action of $\mathcal{I}_3$ on the Bestvina-Bux-Margalit complex of minimizing cycles and with the actions on certain auxiliary complexes of the stabilizers of two- and three-component multicurves on $\Sigma_3$. The remaining ingredients are Tavgen's theorem, which asserts that $\mathrm{Sp}_{6}(\mathbb{Z})$ has bounded elementary generation, and the result of Kassabov and Putman, which asserts that $H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely generated as a $\mathbb{Z}[\mathrm{Sp}_6(\mathbb{Z})]$-module.

papers.title: Homotopy Classification of Pointed Self-Maps of $\mathbb{RP}^3\#\mathbb{RP}^3$
papers.abstract: We classify pointed self-maps of $M=\mathbb{RP}^{3}\#\mathbb{RP}^{3}$ up to pointed homotopy. Using the universal cover $S^2\times\mathbb R$, we reduce the problem to paths in the sphere mapping space with even or odd endpoint conditions. The evaluation fibration, Whitehead products, and a double-coset calculation determine the resulting secondary invariants. The classes inducing the trivial fundamental-group endomorphism split into four families, each in bijection with $\mathbb Z$ after choosing a reference homotopy class. Every other realizable endomorphism sends both standard generators to reflections. For each such endomorphism, the realizable multipliers on $\pi_2(M)\cong\mathbb{Z}$ are precisely the odd integers $d$, and the classes with fixed multiplier are in bijection with $\mathbb Z/|d|\mathbb Z$ after choosing a reference homotopy class. We compute an explicit composition law on the double-reflection submonoid and determine the pointed self-homotopy equivalences. The classes inducing the trivial fundamental-group endomorphism form a subset $\mathcal{T}$ that is preserved by composition on either side with arbitrary pointed homotopy classes and satisfies $\mathcal{T}^2=\{0\}$, where $0$ is the constant class. For each fixed triple $(m,k,d)$ in the double-reflection case, the $|d|$ classes induce identical homomorphisms on every homotopy group. Thus the secondary invariant detects distinctions invisible to these induced homomorphisms.

papers.title: $\ell^p$-Busemann space and the coarse Novikov conjecture
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of an \(\ell^p\)-Busemann space, which is a complete Busemann convex geodesic metric space whose tangent cones admit uniformly controlled homogeneous bi-Lipschitz embeddings into \(\ell^p\)-spaces. An \(\ell^p\)-Busemann space is called admissible if it contains dense sequences of closed convex subsets isometric to certain Finsler manifolds. We then prove that the rational coarse Novikov conjecture holds for proper metric spaces with bounded geometry that admit coarse embeddings into admissible \(\ell^p\)-Busemann spaces.

papers.title: Borel--Serre Callias Classes and Cuspidal Localization
papers.abstract: We construct equivariant Callias classes on the Borel--Serre space of a Hilbert modular group and prove a Kasparov product formula. For torsion-free normal congruence subgroups and twists by powers $m_j\geq2$ of the holomorphic cotangent line bundles, we identify the image of the maximal higher index in the representation ring of the finite quotient with the equivariant index of the cuspidal Dolbeault operator on total forms. The comparison uses a Fredholm homotopy that separates an invertible noncuspidal block. As an application, we compute the $A_5$-equivariant index on the principal level-two Hilbert modular surface over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)$ for all parallel powers $m\geq2$. The resulting class in $R(A_5)$ is $15$-periodic in $m$ and has virtual dimension four. We express this class as an alternating sum of Hilbert cusp-form representations and deduce dimension identities for the full Hilbert modular group.

papers.title: Finite-summability in the noncommutative geometry of crossed products
papers.abstract: We study finite-summability of unbounded representatives of $K$-homology classes for crossed-product $C^*$-algebras associated with actions on compact spaces. Using Kasparov's Dirac--dual-Dirac method, we isolate geometric conditions on the $\gamma$-element under which elements of $K$-homology can be transferred to a crossed product associated with a proper action and represented by finitely summable unbounded cycles defined from Dirac-type operators with an unbounded potential. We relate finite-summability of these operators to integrability properties of the potential by spectral estimates for Schr\"odinger operators on manifolds of bounded geometry. In particular, for finitely generated nilpotent groups this leads to finitely summable, unbounded representatives of all $K$-homology classes. We also give examples showing that representability of $K$-homology classes by finitely summable unbounded cycles is not invariant under $KK$-equivalence.

papers.title: Property A and the identification of the maximal and reduced uniform Roe algebras
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a discrete metric space of bounded geometry. We prove that $X$ has property A if and only if the canonical map $$\lambda:C^*_{u,max}(X)\to C^*_u(X)$$ is an isomorphism.

papers.title: The conductors of fibered Burnside rings
papers.abstract: We give an explicit formula for the conductors of the primitive idempotents of fibered Burnside algebras of finite rank. This formula generalizes previous results for Burnside rings, monomial representation rings, and cyclic fibers, removing the coprimality condition required in the latter case. We also derive some consequences for cyclic fiber groups and $p$-groups.

papers.title: $G$-Hilbert schemes of canonical abelian quotient threefolds
papers.abstract: Ishida and Iwashita showed that the canonical abelian quotient singularities of dimension three that are not Gorenstein fall into four families. For the two families that have not been treated before, we extend a method of K\k{e}dzierski and compute the toric charts of the $G$-Hilbert scheme explicitly. As a result, we show that the $G$-Hilbert scheme has at worst conifold singularities. Combined with known results, this shows that for every three-dimensional canonical abelian quotient singularity, the $G$-Hilbert scheme has at worst conifold singularities, every essential divisor over the singularity appears on it as a prime divisor, and its limit F-blowup is a resolution of the singularity. These results also hold for every three-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial canonical toric singularity in any characteristic, if we replace the $G$-Hilbert scheme by the limit F-blowup of the singularity.

papers.title: A biregular classification of smooth quotients of abelian surfaces
papers.abstract: We classify smooth projective surfaces that are quotients of abelian surfaces by finite groups. We also record the orbifold boundary associated to a quotient map and describe its structure explicitly in the case of augmented irregularity one.

papers.title: A characterisation of almost gentle algebras
papers.abstract: A finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field is gentle if and only if its trivial extension is special biserial. We prove the corresponding characterisation for almost gentle algebras, that is, an algebra over such a field is almost gentle if and only if its trivial extension is special multiserial, which answers a question of Green and Schroll. As a consequence, the property of having a special multiserial trivial extension is invariant under stable equivalence.

papers.title: A geometric approach to the uniform boundedness of $\ell$-primary torsion points
papers.abstract:
We prove that for a non-isotrivial abelian scheme over a smooth curve, the genus of a generic sequence of multi-sections with small heights tends to infinity.
  As an application, we give a new proof of the uniform boundedness of $\ell$-primary torsion points on fibers of an abelian scheme over a smooth curve, a result originally proved by Cadoret and Tamagawa. Furthermore, our approach allows us to reprove a conjecture of Cadoret and Tamagawa without additional assumptions.
  Our approach is based on the theory of Betti foliations and the arithmetic equidistribution theorem.

papers.title: A new proof of the Murnaghan--Nakayama-type rule for stable Grothendieck polynomials of Grassmannian type
papers.abstract: In this article, we present a new proof the Murnaghan--Nakayama-type rule for the stable Grothendieck polynomials of Grassmannian type, which was originally established by Nguyen--Hiep--Son--Thuy.

papers.title: A note on finite length for $\mathrm{GL}_2$
papers.abstract: Let $p>2$ be a prime and $F/\mathbf{Q}_p$ be a finite extension. We prove that every admissible smooth mod $p$ representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$, with a central character, and satisfying a Casimir annihilation condition, has finite length.

papers.title: A Solution to the Birkhoff Problem
papers.abstract: For a commutative uniserial ring $R$ of length $n$ we describe the indecomposable objects in the monomorphism category of $R$ independent of the specific ring for $n\leq 5$ and only dependent on the residue field for $n = 6$. Thus, the classification problem for the monomorphism category of $\mathbb{Z}/p^6 \mathbb{Z}$ reduces to the known case of $\mathbb{F}_p[x]/(x^6)$, resolving the Birkhoff Problem.

papers.title: A Super Version of a Theorem of Fricke-Klein
papers.abstract: We start studying the character variety of the algebraic supergroup OSp(1|2) from the algebraic perspective. We do this by first investigating the specific case of the character variety of the free group on two letters and try to describe the ring of invariants with respect to the conjugation action. The explicit description of the corresponding character variety for SL(2) was done by Fricke and Klein, so this can be seen as a variant of this theorem for its supergeometric counterpart OSp(1|2) and briefly touch upon the character stack for OSp(1|2)

papers.title: Almost-simple algebraic supergroups
papers.abstract: We investigate certain almost-simple algebraic supergroups over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero or odd characteristic. Beyond those whose Lie superalgebras are simple and appear in Kac's classification, we construct new families of almost-simple supergroups whose Lie superalgebras are either non-simple or simple but fall outside Kac's classification.

papers.title: An analogue of irreducible cuspidal representations for the group $PGL(2)$ over a two-dimensional local field
papers.abstract:
Let $F$ be a local non-archimedian field of odd residue characteristic and let $G=PGL(2)$. In this paper we study an analog of irreducible cuspidal representations of the group $G(F)$ when $F$ is replaced by the field $K=F((t))$. The story turns out to be similar to the classical case, but also with some differences. We present a construction of such representations essentially (up to a small subtlety) starting from a quadratic extension $L$ of $K$ and a character $\theta:L^*/K^*\to \mathbb C^*$ which is not Galois invariant. We also show that the restriction of the representations we construct to the group $P(K)$ (here $P$ is a Borel subgroup of $PGL(2)$) is irreducible. However, contrary to the classical case it turns out that these restrictions are not isomorphic to the "standard" irreducible cuspidal representation of $P(K)$.
  In the Appendix we propose a notion of cuspidality for smooth representations of the group $H(K)$ for an arbitrary split reductive group $H$.

papers.title: Approximating parametric suprema for constructible and power-constructible functions
papers.abstract: We prove that one may approximate parametric suprema of constructible and power-constructible functions using functions within the same class. This resolves a conjecture by Adiceam and Cluckers, which was posited after studying a question posed by Sarnak. We apply our result to prove that a certain subclass of Cexp-class distributions is tempered and to make uniform a bound concerning pushforward measures.

papers.title: Arithmetical Foundations - Recursion. Evaluation. Consistency
papers.abstract:
We fix constructive foundations for Arithmetic on a map theoretical, algorithmic level. In contrast to elementhood and quantification based traditional foundations such as Principia Mathematica PM, Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory ZF, or v. Neumann-Goedel-Bernays set theory NGB, our fundamental primitive recursive theory PR has as its basic "undefined" (not further defined) terms just terms for objects and maps. Goodstein's axiomatic uniqueness rules are derived as theorems in PR - with equality definability as a side result -, S is obtained by predicate comprehension, and the equivalence of the theory of partially defined maps and the categorical theory of mu-recursion identifies mu-recursive maps and while-loops with partially defined maps.
  Keywords: Goedel theorems, primitive recursion, categorical free-variables Arithmetic, mu-recursion, totality

papers.title: Belavin--Drinfeld bivectors and Poisson deformations
papers.abstract: We study Belavin--Drinfeld Poisson bivectors $\pi_{(\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^r,\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^c)}$ on $\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m}(\mathbb{C})$ from the perspective of Poisson deformation theory. We prove that the log-canonical part $\pi_0$ of $\pi_{(\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^r,\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^c)}$ is $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbf{\Gamma}^r,\mathbf{\Gamma}^c)}$-log-symplectic if and only if the pair $(\mathbf{\Gamma}^r,\mathbf{\Gamma}^c)$ of Belavin--Drinfeld triples is aperiodic. In this case, we show that $\pi_{(\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^r,\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^c)}$ is a maximal $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbf{\Gamma}^r,\mathbf{\Gamma}^c)}$-invariant Poisson deformation of $\pi_0$, and we construct a $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbf{\Gamma}^r,\mathbf{\Gamma}^c)}$-equivariant Poisson birational map between $(\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m},\pi_0)$ and $(\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m},\pi_{(\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^r,\bar{\mathbf{\Gamma}}^c)})$.

papers.title: Beyond Finite Dimensions: Duflo-Serganova Cohomology, the Formal Superdimension, and a Kac-Wakimoto Theorem for Unitarizable Supermodules
papers.abstract: The main results of this manuscript are fourfold. First, we introduce relative holomorphic discrete series supermodules over basic classical Lie superalgebras $\mathfrak{g}$ and $\mathfrak{sl}(n\vert n)$. These are unitarizable highest weight supermodules whose $\mathfrak{g}_{\bar{0}}$-constituents are Harish-Chandra modules of relative holomorphic discrete series representations. We show that these are exactly the unitarizable highest weight supermodules whose globalizations have supermatrix coefficients square-integrable modulo the center. Second, we define the formal superdimension of a relative holomorphic discrete series supermodule as the parity-weighted sum of the formal dimensions of its $\mathfrak{g}_{\bar{0}}$-constituents. We show that it equals, up to sign, the value at zero of an $L$-packet supercharacter obtained by averaging over the Weyl group. Third, we prove a Kac-Wakimoto theorem for formal superdimension: it is nonzero if and only if the highest weight is maximally atypical. For integral highest weights, it equals the superdimension of a finite-dimensional simple supermodule with the same degree of atypicality. We realize these supermodules through derived Zuckerman functors. For nonintegral highest weights, it is computed by generalized Duflo-Serganova cohomology. Finally, to establish the Kac-Wakimoto conjecture, we develop the theory of generalized Duflo-Serganova cohomology for unitarizable supermodules. We prove that the cohomology of a unitarizable simple supermodule is unitarizable and either zero or simple.

papers.title: Bi-Lipschitz right-left equivalence of finite plane-to-plane germs
papers.abstract: We show that the bi-Lipschitz right-left equivalence of finite holomorphic map germs $(\mathbb{C}^2,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^2,0)$ admits continuous moduli, already among finitely determined polynomial germs of corank one and degree five. The moduli come from a new invariant of finite germs: for two tangent branches of the critical set whose images are tangent, the limit of the ratio of the norms of the images of nearby points is preserved by bi-Lipschitz right-left equivalence. For germs $(F,H)$ with quasihomogeneous components the invariant is computed from the height functions of $F$ and $H$: it is given by the moduli of the values of the height function of the component of lower weighted degree at the roots of a weighted Wronskian. As a first application we obtain a continuous invariant for the germs $(Y^3+3tYX^4+X^6,\,X^N)$, $N\ge7$, built from the Henry--Parusi\'nski family.

papers.title: Campana separable rational connectedness of toric orbifold
papers.abstract: Campana introduced a notion of Campana rational connectedness for Campana orbifolds and conjectured that certain Fano orbifolds are Campana rationally connected. In this paper, we study a version of this conjecture in positive characteristic and verify a stronger statement for some toric orbifolds. We also provide examples illustrating the relation between the failure of separable Campana rational connectedness and singularities.

papers.title: Canonical activation patterns and ReLU pattern varieties
papers.abstract: A ReLU pattern variety records the polynomial relations among the coefficients of the affine maps associated with a prescribed set of activation patterns of a ReLU network. We study how the combinatorics of the canonical set of activation patterns of an unbiased ReLU network is reflected in the geometry of its pattern variety. In particular, we introduce the notion of pattern stability and characterize pattern stability and combinatorial stability for shallow networks. When the associated wall graph is connected and contains an edge of every neuron label, we resolve a problem of Alexandr and Mont\'ufar by determining the defining ideal of the associated pattern variety explicitly. We establish a hierarchy of progressively weaker equivalence relations relating labeled combinatorial equivalence, equality and permutation equivalence of canonical pattern sets, and equivalences of the associated varieties. Finally, we relate functional dimension to the differential of the pattern map and show that it is bounded above by the dimension of the canonical pattern variety at every depth. For nondegenerate shallow networks, we give an exact formula for the functional dimension; for every shallow architecture, it equals the dimension of the canonical pattern variety on an open dense set of full Lebesgue measure.

papers.title: Canonical metrics on punctured spheres, II: compactified moduli spaces of black holes
papers.abstract:
Let $g_{\mathfrak{p}_{\ell}}$ denote the canonical scalar-flat metric on $S^n\setminus \mathfrak{p}_{\ell}$ introduced in Part~I, which for $n=3$ corresponds to the Brill--Lindquist initial data for $\ell$ black holes, and let $\eta\in H_{\ell}$ be its associated mass matrix. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of the metrics and the mass matrix $\eta$ as subsets of punctures collide. Such collisions cause every mass to diverge; if a cluster $A$ of black holes collapses at a relative scale $t$, the mass matrix satisfies $\eta=E(A)\ln(1/t)+O(1)$, diverging along an explicit ray $E(A)\in H_{\ell}$. For nested families of clusters, this degeneracy structure naturally organizes into a space of rooted trees. Subtracting the divergence gives a renormalized mass matrix which extends smoothly to every stratum of the Axelrod--Singer compactified moduli space $\overline{M}{}^{\,\mathrm{AS}}_\ell= \overline C_{\ell-1}(\mathbb{R}^n)/\mathrm O(n)$ and splits naturally into one mass matrix per vertex of the bubble tree.
  Geometrically, at each vertex carrying punctures the suitably rescaled metrics converge to a complete scalar-flat metric with the nodes filled in, adjacent such pieces being joined by Schwarzschild necks, and the renormalized matrix acting as its mass data. For $n=3$, the necks contain minimal spheres, which are common apparent horizons of the merging holes. At vertices bearing two holes, we determine on which side of the limiting horizon each node lies, and we formulate as a conjecture the resulting criterion for a neck to be a component of the outermost horizon. We also compare the mass lower bound of Part~I with the Riemannian Penrose inequality. Because the mass matrix is invariant under rotations of the bubbles, it lives on a Deligne--Mumford-type quotient of the compactification.

papers.title: Cartesian Gray-Monoidal Double Categories
papers.abstract: In this paper we present cartesian structure for symmetric Gray-monoidal double categories. To do this we first introduce locally cubical Gray categories, which are three-dimensional categorical structures analogous to classical, locally globular, Gray categories. The motivating example comprises double categories themselves, together with their functors, transformations, and modifications. A one-object locally cubical Gray category is a Gray-monoidal double category. Braiding, syllepsis, and symmetry for these is introduced in a manner analogous to that for 2-categories. Adding cartesian structure requires the introduction of doubly-lax functors of double categories to manage the order of copies. The resulting theory is algebraically rather complex, largely due to the bureaucracy of linearizing higher-dimensional boundary constraints. Fortunately, it has a relatively simple and compelling representation in the graphical calculus of surface diagrams, which we present.

papers.title: Categorical structures of Kuranishi spaces with $L_{\infty}[1]$-algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce $L_{\infty}$-Kuranishi spaces by associating, to each chart, $L_{\infty}[1]$-algebras defined on open neighborhoods of points in the zero locus of the Kuranishi section. We show that these objects collectively form a category into which the category of smooth manifolds naturally embeds. Some notions in \cite{FOOO1} are modified to achieve the desired categorical structures; for instance, the tangent bundle condition for chart embeddings is replaced by a quasi-isomorphism condition for the $L_{\infty}[1]$-structures.

papers.title: Character variety of the punctured sphere and the determinantal variety
papers.abstract: We show that the SL(2;C) character variety of the n-punctured sphere is described via the determinantal variety defined by an n x n symmetric matrix of rank at most 4 whose entries are the traces of simple closed curves on the surface. This result generalizes the Fricke-Klein-Vogt relations to arbitrary n, and we determine the structure of the kernel of the associated matrix.

papers.title: Chern bounds and tangent geometry of polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds
papers.abstract: We study the numerical geography and tangent geometry of very amply polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds $(X,H)$ through the positivity of the first jet bundle $J^1(H)$. Let $d=\int_X H^3$, $c=\int_Xc_2(X) H$, and $e=\int_X c_3(X)$. We obtain $e\ge-5d-c-c^2/(4d)$ by mixed intersections on $\mathbb{P}(J^1(H)^*)$, and $e\ge40d\left[(1-\frac{c}{10d})^{3/2}-1\right]$ by a volume estimate for a perturbed tautological class. In particular, the latter inequality shows $e+6c\ge0$, improving Sun's inequality $e+10c\ge0$. As consequences, we show (1) the uniform Hodge bounds $-4d-80\le h^{1,1}(X)-h^{2,1}(X)\le173d/66$, (2) the lower bound $\mathrm{deg} X^\vee\ge78$ for the dual hypersurface, and (3) the upper bound $d\le34$ in the critical case $X\subset\mathbb{P}^6$.

papers.title: Classification of ${\rm GL}_1(D)\times {\rm GL}_{n-1}(D)$-distinguished representations
papers.abstract:
Let $D$ be a quaternion division algebra over a non-Archimedean
  local field $F$ of characteristic zero.
  We prove the conjecture of Dagar, Sharma, and Verma classifying irreducible smooth
  representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(D)$ distinguished by
  $\mathrm{GL}_1(D)\times\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(D)$ for $n>2$.
  These are precisely the trivial representation and the
  irreducible normalized parabolic inductions
  $\one_{n-2}\times\tau$, where $\tau$ is an infinite-dimensional
  irreducible representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(D)$ distinguished
  by $\mathrm{GL}_1(D)\times\mathrm{GL}_1(D)$.
  The proof combines a choice of cuspidal inducing factor
  with orbit conditions and multisegment methods.

papers.title: Classification of real nodal orders
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study properties of nodal orders defined over arbitrary base fields. In particular we give a classification of complete real nodal orders.

papers.title: Compactly supported $p$-adic pro-\'etale cohomology of analytic varieties
papers.abstract: We study properties of compactly supported $p$-adic pro-\'etale cohomology of smooth partially proper rigid analytic varieties. In particular, we prove a comparison theorem, in a stable range, with compactly supported syntomic cohomology, which is built from compactly supported Hyodo-Kato and ${\mathcal B}^+_{\rm dr}$-cohomologies. We derive from that a (limited version of a) fundamental diagram.

papers.title: Computer-assisted proofs for the fourth algebraic transfer in certain generic degrees
papers.abstract: This paper restructures the author's earlier article in Journal of Homotopy and Related Structures to correct its erroneous invariant-dimension calculations for the fourth Singer algebraic transfer and is written as a replacement for that article. More precisely, we determine the domain and image of the transfer in the degree families $2^{s+t+1}+2^{s+1}-3$ with $t\ne3$ and $2^{s+t}+2^s-2$ with $t\notin\{2,3,4\}$, where $s,t$ are positive integers. Divided-power spikes are basis elements dual to polynomial monomials whose exponents have the form $2^j-1$ for nonnegative integers $j$. Their translates under ${\rm GL}_4(\mathbb F_2)$, the group of invertible $4\times4$ matrices over the field with two elements, generate submodules of the Steenrod kernel, the subspace annihilated by all positive Steenrod squares. We present these submodules as quotients of sums of permutation modules on complete flags, which are chains in $\mathbb F_2^4$ containing one subspace of each dimension $0,1,2,3,4$. Identifying the relation spaces in these presentations gives explicit equivariant comparison isomorphisms. A recursion obtained by separating even and odd exponents in each variable reduces the comparisons to specified identities of finite-dimensional subspaces. These comparisons apply to both complete degree families, including the parameter values omitted from the transfer theorem. Duplication and partial flag embeddings also give theoretical comparisons in specified parameter ranges. As a consequence, Singer's injectivity conjecture holds in rank four in both degree families under the stated parameter restrictions. The cokernel is one-dimensional in homological degree $256$ and zero in every other degree in those ranges.

papers.title: Consecutive primes at distances 123,662 and 125,318
papers.abstract: We exhibit consecutive-prime gaps of exactly $123\,662$ and $125\,318$, with endpoints of $8\,416$ and $6\,454$ decimal digits, respectively. Covering congruences certify most interior integers as composite. For the second gap, the remaining integers are certified by proper divisors or Fermat witnesses. Elliptic-curve certificates prove all four endpoints prime. We give the elementary arguments that turn these finite arithmetic checks into a proof. The proof is computer-assisted.

papers.title: Constructing high-dimensional representations of twin groups via several techniques
papers.abstract: In this article, we consider the twin group $T_n$ for a positive integer $n$ and present two techniques for constructing high-dimensional and complicated representations of $T_n$. The first technique consists of composing a known representation of $T_n$ with the well-established Cohen map, while the second technique relies on the tensor product of two known representations of $T_n$. To implement these techniques, we consider the two representations $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$ of $T_n$ introduced recently by Nasser. The first technique is applied to the representation $\eta_1: T_n \longrightarrow \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{F}_n)$, which maps $T_n$ into the automorphism group of the free group $\mathbb{F}_n$ with $n$ generators. The second technique is applied to the representation $\eta_2: T_n \longrightarrow \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z}[t^{\pm 1}])$, which maps $T_n$ into the general linear group over the ring of Laurent polynomials in an indeterminate $t$. Using these techniques, we construct new high-degree representations of $T_n$ and examine, for some of them, structural properties such as faithfulness and reducibility. This work provides new avenues for developing representations of $T_n$ and related groups using these techniques.

papers.title: Cotorsion pairs in $\eta$-extensions with applications to $\theta$-extension rings and tensor rings
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal B$ be an abelian category with enough projective and injective objects, and let $\mathcal B\ltimes_\eta F$ be an $\eta$-extension of $\mathcal B$ with $\eta$ associative. Given a cotorsion pair $(\mathcal X, \mathcal Y)$ in $\mathcal B$, we show that the cotorsion pair $(\Delta(\mathcal X),\Delta(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ exists for arbitrary associative $\eta$, removing the square-zero assumption $F^2=0$ from Hu's construction. When $(\mathcal X, \mathcal Y)$ is hereditary, the heredity of $(\Delta(\mathcal X),\Delta(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ is characterized by the first left derived functor of a canonical defect functor $\delta$. We also remark that Hu's construction and hereditary result for the cotorsion pair $({}^\perp U^{-1}(\mathcal Y), U^{-1}(\mathcal Y))$ remain valid without the nilpotence assumption on $\eta$. Under nilpotence hypotheses, we establish a completeness criterion for $(\Delta(\mathcal X),\Delta(\mathcal X)^\perp)$ using the Beligiannis radical functor $\mathfrak r$. And we also provide a completeness criterion for $({}^\perp U^{-1}(\mathcal Y), U^{-1}(\mathcal Y))$ if $\mathcal B\ltimes_\eta F$ has enough injective objects. We give sufficient conditions for their coincidence. Dual results are obtained for $\zeta$-coextensions. Finally, we specialize the theory to $\theta$-extension rings and tensor rings, where the abstract conditions admit explicit module-theoretic descriptions.

papers.title: Counterexamples to Green's Conjecture via E_6-covers
papers.abstract: We show that curves of genus 10 which are W(E_6)-covers of the projective line provide counterexamples to Green's Conjecture on syzygies of canonical curves. This leads to a 9-dimensional family of explicit counterexamples to Green's Conjecture. We also show that the same curves provide counterexamples to the Green-Lazarsfeld Secant Conjecture. Both Green's Conjecture and the Secant Conjecture are know to be true in the generic case, as well as in many other situations.

papers.title: Counting Matrices of Prescribed Jordan Type in Incidence Algebras
papers.abstract: We count nilpotent matrices in the incidence algebra of a finite poset over a finite field that belong to a prescribed conjugacy class for the adjoint action of the general linear group. We prove that these counts depend only on the comparability graph of the poset. We introduce shuffle-prefix posets, a class containing all finite interval orders, and give explicit formulas for their nilpotent Jordan counts. These counts are polynomials with integer coefficients in the field size, valid over every finite field. Finally, Fourier duality relates conjugacy-class counts in a coordinate subspace to those in the subspace supported on the complementary matrix positions, whenever one subspace consists entirely of nilpotent matrices.

papers.title: Counting real meromorphic differentials on $\mathbb{CP}^1$
papers.abstract: The counting problem for meromorphic differentials on $\mathbb{CP}^1$ with fixed orders of zeros and poles and vanishing residues at some specific poles, up to the action of $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ and the multiplication by a nonzero constant, was completely solved before by several authors. In all the cases when there are finitely many such meromorphic differentials, an explicit formula for their number was found and also, in the case of residueless meromorphic differentials with two zeros, a link to the WDVV equations and the KP hierarchy was established. We consider a real analog of these counting problems by requiring that a meromorphic differential is preserved by a real structure on $\mathbb{CP}^1$. Our real counting problems admit refinements, obtained for example by specifying the orders of poles and zeros that are fixed by the antiholomorphic involution. We obtain explicit formulas for all our real counting problems and also, in the case of real meromorphic differentials with two complex conjugate zeros and residueless poles, establish a link to the open WDVV equations and the system of equations for the wave function of the KP hierarchy. An application to real Hurwitz numbers is also presented.

papers.title: Cycles on the universal moduli of rank 2 bundles over the hyperelliptic locus
papers.abstract: We establish a strong Franchetta property for the universal moduli stack of rank two vector bundles over smooth hyperelliptic curves and identify the image of the Chow ring in the cohomology of a fiber via restriction and the cycle class map as precisely the monodromy invariant cohomology classes. More precisely, for every genus $g\geq 2$, degree $d$, and hyperelliptic curve $C$ of genus $g$, we show that the restriction and the cycle class map identifies the Chow ring of the universal moduli stack with the subring of $H^* (Bun_{2,d}(C),\mathbb Q)$ generated by twisted $\kappa$-classes, which coincides with $H^{*}(Bun_{2,d}(C), \mathbb Q)^{\pi_1(\mathcal H_g,[C])}$. We use this viewpoint to give an alternative proof to a theorem of Larson in (arXiv:2404.12607), and verify a conjecture of the second author in (arXiv:2604.11958) in the rank $2$ case.

papers.title: Decompositions of the diagonal of complete intersections in products of projective spaces
papers.abstract: We study rationality of very general complete intersections in products of projective spaces. By constructing specific reference varieties and apply specialization method in the form of relative torsion orders, we extend the quintic constructions by Hotchkiss and the quartic constructions by B\"ohning, Graf von Bothmer, Pirutka and Zhang to very general complete intersections in products in every characteristic. In particular, we prove that very general quartic hypersurfaces of positive dimension admit no decomposition of the diagonal in every characteristic.

papers.title: Deligne pairing isomorphisms for projective duals and higher-rank associated hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: Given a family \pi:X\to S of complex projective varieties, polarised by a (sufficiently) relatively very ample L, we give an isomorphism between a Deligne pairing involving higher relative cotangent Chern classes, and the relative projective dual line X^\vee(L). As a consequence, we obtain explicit Deligne pairing isomorphisms for all of the higher associated hypersurfaces of Gelfand--Kapranov--Zelevinsky, including mixed polarisations, as well as higher-rank versions of such hypersurfaces involving sufficiently positive vector bundles.

papers.title: Derived sheaves in locally conformally symplectic geometry
papers.abstract: In this paper, we use derived sheaves to study rigidity phenomena in the cotangent bundles of manifolds endowed with some locally conformally symplectic ($\frak{lcs}$) structure. Taking inspiration from the work of Guillermou, Kashiwara and Shapira, we define a quantization for ``$\frak{lcs}$'' Hamiltonian isotopies, as well as new quantities: the asymptotic Betti numbers of a sheaf. We then show that those quantities are ``well behaved'' with respect of said quantization and use this to give a sheaf-theoretical proof of the Chantraine-Murphy theorem. We also consider the quantization in light of the Tamarkin morphism and the displacement energy of sheaves. This allows us to derive a non-squeezing theorem for $\frak{lcs}$ geometry that is similar, although not identical, to the one recently proven by Bertelson, Chakravarthy, and Sandon. Indeed, the result shown in this paper is more in line with the contact non-squeezing theorem shown by Eliashberg, Kim and Polterovich in 2006.

papers.title: Diameters of the order and chain polytopes of a connected poset
papers.abstract: For a finite poset $P$, Stanley's order polytope $\mathcal O(P)$ and chain polytope $\mathcal C(P)$ have the same number of vertices and, by a theorem of Hibi, Li, Sahara and Shikama, the same number of edges. On disconnected posets the diameters of their graphs can differ by any amount, since both diameters add over disjoint unions and already differ on small examples, but on connected posets a computer search of Lee found no difference larger than $1$. We show that on connected posets, too, the two diameters can be far apart. For every $k\ge1$ we describe a connected poset $B_k$ with $3k$ elements whose order polytope has graph diameter $k$ and whose chain polytope has graph diameter at most $\lfloor3(k+1)/4\rfloor$; hence the first diameter can exceed the second by any amount. For every $n\ge4$ we construct a connected poset $P_n$ with $2n^2+5n+1$ elements whose order polytope has graph diameter $2$ and whose chain polytope has graph diameter $4$. Finally, for every finite poset $P$, if the graph of $\mathcal O(P)$ has diameter at most $2$, then the graph of $\mathcal C(P)$ has diameter at most $4$; so $2$ is the largest possible difference when the order polytope has graph diameter $2$.

papers.title: Distributivity, affineness, and the structure sheaf
papers.abstract: We observe that for a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme the structure sheaf generates the perfect complexes if and only if the lattice of thick subcategories is distributive if and only if the affinization map is 0-affine. Examples are discussed, including an example of a quasi-projective scheme which is not quasi-affine but for which these equivalent conditions hold.

papers.title: Elliptic Gromov-Witten Invariants of Instanton Moduli
papers.abstract:
We calculate the genus $1$ Gromov-Witten invariants with one tautological divisor insertion of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}(r,n)$ of rank-$r$, $c_2=n$ torsion-free sheaves on $\mathbb{P}^2$ framed along the infinity divisor. As rational functions of the framing parameters, we determine the polar parts of these invariants by exploring the equivariant geometry of the Gieseker-Uhlenbeck map $\mathcal{M}(r,n)\to\mathcal{M}_0(r,n)$. We determine the polynomial part of these invariants by relating their large framing limits to the results \cite{ILPT} for the rank $1$ case, namely $\mathrm{Hilb}^n(\mathbb{C}^2)$. The degree-$0$ invariants with one divisor insertion are evaluated by studying the combinatorics of multi-partitions.
  We also prove reconstruction results for invariants with multiple insertions. Under the assumption that the eigenvalues of the divisor operator are linearly independent as functions of the Novikov variable, these results determine the full genus $1$ theory from the one-divisor series and the genus $0$ divisor operator.

papers.title: Equivariant geometry of quadrics blown-up along a twisted quartic
papers.abstract: We prove that $G$-Fano threefolds which are given by the blow-up of a smooth quadric along a twisted quartic curve are $G$-birationally superrigid if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{A}_5\times\mathbb{Z}_2$. We also prove that the action of $G$ is linearisable if and only if $G$ does not contain a subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$.

papers.title: Equivariant homomorphisms and Mordell--Weil groups of twists of Albanese varieties of cyclic multiple planes
papers.abstract: Let $X'\to X$ be a Galois cover of smooth projective varieties over a field $k$ with group $G$, and let $G$ act on an abelian variety $A$ over $k$. We prove an exact sequence relating the Mordell--Weil group of the twist of $A$ by $k(X')/k(X)$ to the group of $G$-equivariant homomorphisms from the Albanese variety of $X'$ to $A$; the remaining obstruction is killed by $|G|$. This corrects structure theorems in two earlier papers of the author and in a corrigendum to the first, where the equivariance condition was omitted. For the twists of Albanese varieties of cyclic multiple planes considered in those papers, we determine the rank and the torsion subgroup. Over number fields we describe the rank through the Galois action on endomorphisms and prove a specialization result. When $F(x,y)=0$ is the dual of the Fermat cubic, the Mordell curves $y^2=x^3+16F(a,b)$ have rank at least $3$ over $\mathbb Q$ for all $(a,b)\in {\mathbb Q}^2$ outside a thin set.

papers.title: Essential dimension of geometric local systems
papers.abstract: Let f : X → B be a smooth projective family over a smooth complex variety, and let H = (Rmf∗Z)/tors. We prove that there is an integer N such that, whenever pn ≥N, the essential dimension at p of H/pn is at least the dimension of its period image. This proves the Brosnan–Fakhruddin conjecture for these local systems. The proof compares the geometric Sen operator with the Higgs field. Integral Hodge–Tate theory gives a bound uniform in large primes. For each remaining prime, a bounded rational comparison at one geometric point suffices when n is large.

papers.title: Even Asymptotic Expansions and Uniform Hard-Edge Approximations for Wigner $3j$ and $6j$ Symbols at Fixed Rank
papers.abstract: We study Wigner $3j$ symbols with two large and one small angular momentum, and the $6j$ symbols with one small entry (Edmonds' limit), both at fixed rank: the small labels stay fixed while the large ones grow. Their classical limits are Wigner rotation matrix elements. Combining a Regge symmetry with the Weyl shift $j\mapsto j+\tfrac12$ singles out midpoint variables: for $3j$, the large scale $N=j_-+j_++1$ ($j_\mp$ the two large angular momenta) and $x=2\mu/N$ ($2\mu$ the difference of the two large magnetic indices), and, for $6j$, large lengths $A,B,C$ shifted by offsets that depend on the small labels. Among constant shifts of the large labels and magnetic coordinate, and up to rank-independent gauge factors, these are the only centerings that remove the generic first-order term of the exact recurrences. In these variables the normalized symbols are values of analytic functions of the inverse square of the large scale, for integer and half-integer small labels alike (including spin–orbit coefficients): the expansions contain only even powers and converge. The first correction is a closed formula in one Wigner $d$ function and its derivative, improving the error from second to fourth order in the inverse large scale; all higher corrections are constructed as local differential operators. The exact finite problems are Hahn and Racah spectral systems with undeformed Wigner spectra. Near the ends of the physical lattice (the hard edges), an explicit product of Pochhammer factors carries the difference between the discrete and continuum weights; extracting it gives expansions that are uniform on the whole lattice, including the $6j$ corner where two large lengths nearly coincide ($A\approx B$). We also show that centered Hahn and Racah polynomials are even deformations of Jacobi polynomials.

papers.title: Explicit cohomological transfer for Morita equivalent Lie groupoids
papers.abstract:
It is well known that Morita equivalent Lie groupoids have isomorphic differentiable cohomology. At the cochain level, however, explicitly transporting a cocycle from one groupoid to a Morita equivalent one is less straightforward.
  We provide explicit formulas for such cohomological transfers in arbitrary degree. More precisely, for the pullback of a Lie groupoid along a surjective submersion, we construct an explicit cochain-level homotopy inverse to the natural pullback map. We first treat \v{C}ech groupoids, where the construction only involves a partition of unity, and then extend it to arbitrary surjective submersions, for which the extra choice of local sections is needed.
  We also show that the resulting operators preserve the complexes associated with $\mathcal{VB}$-groupoids, including homogeneous and $\mathcal{VB}$-cochains. As an application, we obtain explicit transfer maps for deformation cocycles of Morita equivalent Lie groupoids and recover the Morita invariance of deformation cohomology.

papers.title: Exterior power operations on relative K-theory
papers.abstract: We algebraically construct exterior power operations on higher relative algebraic K-groups and prove their desired properties such as the expected behaviour with respect to (tensor) products and composition. This builds on Grayson's description of relative K-groups in terms of explicit generators and relations and on work by Harris, the first author and Taelman for (absolute) K-groups. Among the new features in our approach is the observation that the product axiom in the classical notion of a lambda-ring is redundant.

papers.title: Fano blowups of Grassmannians along sub-Grassmannians
papers.abstract: Let $\tilde X$ be the successive blowup of the Grassmannian $\operatorname{Gr}(d,n+1)$ with $n\ge3$, in arbitrary characteristic, along sub-Grassmannians of codimension $r_1,\dotsc,r_s\ge2$ that meet transversely. We prove that, if $d\ne2$, then $\tilde X$ is Fano if and only if $\sum_i(r_i-1)\le n$, and we give a similar criterion for $d=2$. As applications, we prove that the successive blowup of $\mathbb{P}^4$ along $s$ planes that meet transversely is Fano if and only if $s\le4$. We also determine when the successive blowup of a smooth quadric fourfold along planes of one family that meet transversely is Fano.

papers.title: Far-field prediction of algebraic curves via generalized asymptotes
papers.abstract: The asymptotic behavior of algebraic curves is classically described by means of linear asymptotes. However, many infinite branches exhibit a non-linear behavior that cannot be represented accurately by straight lines. In this paper we propose a computational framework for far-field prediction of algebraic curves based on generalized asymptotes. Starting from the asymptotic expansion of a real branch at infinity, we retain its non-decaying terms in order to construct an algebraic surrogate, which is then used as an adaptive far-field model outside a sufficiently large compact region. We introduce explicit discrepancy indicators and a switching radius that determine when the exact branch may be replaced by its generalized asymptotic predictor. The framework recovers the classical linear asymptote whenever the latter exists, while remaining effective for branches with polynomial or Puiseux-type dominant behavior. In the implicit setting, we prove algebraicity and compatibility properties of the predictor and derive asymptotic error estimates from the first neglected term of the expansion. A residual certificate distinguishes guaranteed finite-tail replacement from asymptotic radius estimates. Tangential tails, slow decay, and a smooth transition rule clarify the limitations of truncation. Reproducible finite-window tests compare the predictors with fitted polynomial baselines; these tests are not a benchmark of a complete plotting system.

papers.title: Fiberwise criteria for Fourier--Mukai equivalences
papers.abstract: We prove fiberwise criteria for full faithfulness and equivalences of integral transforms between proper flat families of schemes over a separated Noetherian base. The kernels are bounded pseudocoherent complexes which are relatively perfect over each factor, and need not be perfect. A key ingredient is the calculus of mates, which controls the units and counits of adjoint integral transforms under base change. In particular, we give a complete argument for a fiberwise criterion of Hern\'{a}ndez Ruip\'{e}rez--L\'{o}pez Mart\'{i}n--Sancho de Salas, and extend it to arbitrary separated Noetherian bases. As applications, we extend a result of Orlov on field extensions to singular varieties, and show that over a Noetherian local ring these properties can be detected on the special fiber.

papers.title: Field algebras associated with non-symmetric lattices
papers.abstract: Field algebras, introduced by Bakalov and Kac, generalize vertex algebras by replacing locality with a weaker associativity-type axiom. We develop the structure theory of field algebras with a view toward geometric examples in which a natural bilinear form fails to be symmetric. We prove a reconstruction theorem for field algebras, producing a field algebra structure from a generating family of fields. We associate to every finite-rank lattice $L$ equipped with an arbitrary bilinear form a canonical field algebra $V_L$, generalizing the Heisenberg and lattice vertex algebras. We then study potential definitions of commutants in this setting and analyze when they are realized as subfield algebras. Finally, we realize these constructions geometrically by looking at the homology of the moduli stack of complexes of quiver representations, extending previous results from Dominic Joyce.

papers.title: Flat and very flat pro-quasi-coherent pro-sheaves on ind-schemes
papers.abstract: This is a paper about homological algebra of flat pro-quasi-coherent pro-sheaves. We recall and collect various techniques such as accessibility and deconstructibility, and adopt them to ind-schemes under various assumptions. We also discuss the foundations of the notion of an ind-scheme.

papers.title: Flow reconfiguration with one modulus for all graphs, and Cereceda's conjecture for bipartite 2-degenerate graphs
papers.abstract: This paper answers a question of Esperet, Hendrey, Lagoutte, Marseloo, Norin and Steiner on flow reconfiguration and makes inroads into Cereceda's recolouring conjecture for $d=2$. Parts I and II are about flows. For a finite multigraph $G$ and an integer $k\ge 2$, let $M_k(G)$ be the graph on the nowhere-zero $\mathbb{Z}_k$-flows of $G$, and $I_k(G)$ the graph on the integer flows $F$ of $G$ with $1\le|F(e)|\le k-1$ on every edge; two flows are adjacent if the support of their difference is a cycle. We prove that $M_k(G)$ and $I_k(G)$ are connected for every finite bridgeless loopless multigraph $G$ if $k=40$, if $k=48$, or if $k$ is a multiple of $4$ with $k\ge 52$. This answers their Problem 1.2. The same holds for $k=66$, for every prime power $p^N$ with $N\ge 6$, and for a set of moduli of natural density one; these results do not cover every $k\ge 40$. A master theorem for finite abelian groups gives the connectivity of the flow graph $F(G,\Gamma)$ for every abelian group $\Gamma$ of order $40$, and a binary form of it for every abelian group of exponent dividing $4$ and order at least $32$, in particular $\mathbb{F}_2^5$ (Esperet et al. proved $\mathbb{F}_2^8$). Part III is about colourings: two proper $k$-colourings of a graph $G$ are adjacent if they differ at exactly one vertex. Cereceda conjectured that this graph has diameter $O(n^2)$ for every $d$-degenerate graph on $n$ vertices and $k=d+2$; the case $d=2$ is open. For four colours we prove the diameter bound $2n(n+1)$ for every bipartite graph of degeneracy at most $2$, with the order $n^2$ sharp in this class, also at girth $6$; the bound $5n(n+1)$ when an independent set of vertices of degree at most $2$ is added; and, with a computer-verified certificate, $4n(n+1)$ for every graph of cone width at most $2$, a class that contains all graphs of treewidth at most $2$ and some graphs of treewidth $3$ with triangles.

papers.title: Folding of d-invariants via F-invariants with applications to quiver Hecke KR-modules
papers.abstract: The \(\de\)-invariant measures the interaction between two simple modules and controls the behavior of their convolution product. Using categorical interpretations of Cao's tropical and \(F\)-invariants, we establish folding formulas for the \(\Lambda\)-invariants between determinantial modules in arbitrary symmetrizable type and derive the corresponding \(\de\)-formula by symmetrization. We apply the \(\de\)-formula to quiver Hecke Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules and show that, in every finite type, their \(\de\)-invariants are completely determined by the coefficients of the symmetrized inverse \(t\)-quantized Cartan matrix. We obtain explicit formulas in all finite types, including closed formulas in the classical types \(A\), \(B\), \(C\), and \(D\).

papers.title: From Four-Dimensional Wilson Lattice Gauge Theory to Quantum Yang--Mills Theory, with a Conditional Mass-Gap Theorem
papers.abstract: We present a complete formal paper compiling the Lean-verified construction of quantum Yang--Mills theory submitted on October 28, 2026, and independently validated by the Yang--Mills Shepherding Committee. Starting from the Wilson definition of lattice gauge theory on a four-dimensional torus, we give full proofs of every step that can be carried out from the definitions: the field-label algebra, the finite lattice theory, and--under an explicit, individually registered package of renormalization-group and analytic assumptions--the fixed-volume ultraviolet limit, the subsequential infinite-volume limit, the phase decomposition with clustering and full support, the Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction satisfying the Wightman axioms, and the Yang--Mills identification: the stress tensor and its Ward identity, the trace anomaly with the verified constant 3 dim_R(g)/pi^4, the exclusion of a precise class of free-field descriptions, the one-loop running coupling, and the operator product expansion. For the mass gap we prove two logical boundaries: an explicit model satisfies all registered inputs with clustering, yet its Hamiltonian has no spectral gap; and a mass gap is equivalent to a uniform exponential rate in the clustering axiom, with the bridge from the volume-uniform transfer-matrix condition to the continuum gap proved. A uniform mass gap requires new infrared input; we develop one explicitly conditional route (semiclassical tunneling in the defining representation of SU(2)), and we prove that, with the registered input set fixed, removing the conditionality is equivalent to proving the mass gap itself. A positive mass gap is not proved.

papers.title: Functor-induced isomorphisms and $G$-matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper, we explore how functor-induced isomorphisms are encoded by $G$-matrices. We first show that the Grothendieck group isomorphism induced by a tilting module can be realized via the $G$-matrix of this tilting module. Building on this, we compare $g$-vectors for a tilted algebra and its associated hereditary algebra, and provide $G$-matrix interpretations of the Coxeter transformation, the Nakayama functor, and the Auslander-Reiten translation for suitable algebras. Furthermore, we demonstrate the geometric representations of any Weyl group can be realized by the $G$-matrices of tilting modules or support $\tau$-tilting modules arising from generalized preprojective algebras. Consequently, the group generated by the transpose of these $G$-matrices is isomorphic to the corresponding Weyl group. Finally, we show that the Grothendieck group isomorphism induced by a $2$-term silting complex can also be realized via the $G$-matrix of this $2$-term silting complex.

papers.title: G-birationally rigid cubic threefolds
papers.abstract: We classify pairs $(X,G)$ consisting of a (possibly singular) cubic threefold $X\subset\mathbb{P}^4$ and a finite subgroup $G\subset\mathrm{Aut}(X)$ such that $X$ is $G$-birationally rigid, i.e., $X$ is a $G$-Mori fiber space (over a point), and $X$ is not $G$-birational to any $G$-Mori fibre space that is not $G$-biregular to $X$.

papers.title: Generic splitting types and Terao's conjecture for seventeen and eighteen lines
papers.abstract: We prove that the generic splitting type of the logarithmic bundle of an arrangement of at most eighteen lines in the complex projective plane is determined by the intersection lattice. In particular, Terao's freeness conjecture holds for seventeen and eighteen lines. For any number of lines, it holds for free arrangements whose smaller exponent is at most eight. By the theorem for at most sixteen lines, the problem reduces to a uniformity condition for lattices of seventeen lines: if all realizations have minimal Jacobian-syzygy degree at least seven, then all or none have degree seven. The proof has two parts. First, a realization of minimal degree seven has defect at most four, the defect being the length of the zero scheme of a minimal section. This uses the residual inflection quartic of the associated degree-seven foliation, local inflection identities, and fixed-point theory for critically fixed rational maps of degree seven with exact finite certificates. Second, the uniformity condition holds at these defects. For multiplicities at most six, a critical realization contains a twelve-line core of minimal weight, and an exact search through extensions of the cores shows that the lattice has a single Galois orbit of realizations; the only family left at defect four has no critical member. For a point of multiplicity seven we use the zero scheme of the pencil derivation and a classification of transversal structures. Terao's conjecture for seventeen and eighteen lines needs only defects one, two and three and, for seventeen lines, this classification at multiplicity seven. The proof is computer-assisted.

papers.title: Geometric structures of $G$-fans associated with rank $3$ cluster-cyclic exchange matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the geometric structures of $G$-fans associated with rank $3$ real cluster-cyclic exchange matrices.
