In this class, a simple recursion for tropical signs was found, which enables us to study the detailed properties of $c$-, $g$-vectors. We introduce two kinds of upper bounds of the $G$-fans. The first one is the global upper bound, which comes from a hyperbolic surface containing all $g$-vectors after an initial mutation. The second one is the local upper bound, which reflects the internal separateness structure. As applications, we prove that there is no periodicity among $g$-vectors, and we completely determine the sign of $g$-vectors. We also prove the monotonicity of $g$-vectors under the minimum assumption. Moreover, we show that the three global upper bounds can be simplified to a single uniform upper bound.

papers.title: Gordan-Rankin-Cohen brackets on $1|n$-dimensional superstrings with a contact structure for $n\leq 6$
papers.abstract:
The binary projectively $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$-invariant differential operators between spaces of weighted densities on the 1-dimensional manifold are called Gordan transvectants or Rankin-Cohen (GRC) brackets. For the two contact series (with an even and an odd ``time'' variable) on the supercircle or superstring of dimension $1|2$, we describe analogs of GRC brackets. We have discovered many new operators. For $\mathfrak{osp}(2|2)\subset\mathfrak{k}(1|2)$, the space of invariant binary operators of every given order is $2$-dimensional for all weights of the densities, not only for the weights considered so far. For $\mathfrak{pe}(2)\subset\mathfrak{m}(1)$, there are three independent binary operators of order $2$, not two. While classifying them, we correct an earlier result on the unary operators: the order-$2$ Bol operator over $\mathfrak{m}(1)$ is only one member of a $1$-parameter family invariant for all weights, which corrects Theorem 5.1 of arXiv:2110.10504.
  We correct earlier findings in the $1|3$-dimensional case and consider $\mathfrak{osp}_a(4|2)$-invariant (GRC) brackets in $1|4$-dimensional case, where the order-$2$ bracket is independent of the parameter $a$ and is invariant under the whole of $\mathfrak{k}(1|4)$. In the $1|5$-dimensional case, the analogs of Bol operators are odd, of order $5+2k$, where $k=0,1,2,\dots$, and so is the first GRC bracket of odd order, which is of order $5$. We also settle the exceptional case $\mathfrak{as}\subset\mathfrak{kas}\subset\mathfrak{k}(1|6)$.

papers.title: Gorenstein toric Fano $d$-varieties have Picard ranks at most $2d$
papers.abstract: We show that the Picard rank of $d$-dimensional Gorenstein toric Fano varieties is at most $2d$. This generalizes Batyrev's conjecture of Picard ranks for smooth toric Fano varieties, which was proved by Casagrande for all $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial Gorenstein toric Fano varieties. The convex-geometric proof is a generalization of Casagrande's proof and Eikelberg's theory of non-$\mathbb{Q}$-factorial toric Picard groups, with key ideas from work of Debarre, {\O}bro, Fujita and the first author. The proof was found using ChatGPT 6.1.

papers.title: Harish-Chandra Modules for the Lie algebra of Divergence-Free Vector Fields on a Two-Dimensional Torus
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal S_2$ be the Lie algebra of divergence-free Laurent polynomial vector fields on a two-dimensional torus. We determine its simple weight modules with uniformly bounded weight multiplicities. As a consequence, we obtain a classification of its simple Harish-Chandra modules, i.e., weight modules with finite-dimensional weight spaces, which are either simple generalized highest weight modules or simple quotients of tensor fields modules.

papers.title: Heavy-Light Wall Crossings and Motivic Asymptotics of Moduli Spaces of Curves. Part II: Tameness of Motivic Measures
papers.abstract:
This paper is concerned with the study of the fixed-genus asymptotics of motivic measures of moduli spaces of stable pointed curves and their minimal all-light Hassett compactifications as the number of markings tends to infinity. A motivic wall-crossing argument gives a universal change of variables between the two generating series, depending only on the value of the Lefschetz class. For an arbitrary motivic measure, we use stabilization graphs and support patterns to express the all-light series in terms of universal chain factors and finite residual quotient families. This formal decomposition isolates the rational trivalent contribution without requiring a fixed-locus formula for finite quotients.
  To pass from formal identities to asymptotics, we formulate analytic hypotheses (the $\mathrm{H}_g$-hypotheses) for scalar realizations with positive real Lefschetz value. We introduce vertex tameness and residual-quotient tameness, whose conjunction, graph tameness, provides geometric sufficient conditions for the $\mathrm{H}_g$-hypotheses. In genus at least two, this yields explicit leading asymptotics in both chambers, depending only on the genus and the Lefschetz value; genera zero and one are treated separately. As an application, we prove graph tameness for Hodge-Deligne evaluations and deduce fixed-product universality and asymptotic concentration of Hodge numbers on the diagonal.

papers.title: Higher cotangent cohomology for Stanley-Reisner rings
papers.abstract: Inspired by work of Altmann and Christophersen, we study the graded pieces of the cotangent cohomology $T^i_{S_{\mathcal{K}}}$, $i\geq 3$ of the Stanley-Reisner ring $S_{\mathcal{K}}$ associated to a simplicial complex $\mathcal{K}$. We prove a localization formula allowing one to reduce to the case of negative weights. Our results give a complete description of $T^3$ and $T^4$ in terms of the topology of $\mathcal{K}$ whenever $\mathcal{K}$ is a flag complex. As an application, we give a sufficient criterion for the vanishing of $T^3$ for simplicial spheres, classify two-spheres that have vanishing $T^3$, and show that the boundary complex of the dual associahedron has vanishing $T^3$. Our results make use of the arborescent resolutions considered by Hancharuk, Laurent-Gengoux, and Strobl. We give an alternative and self-contained treatment of these resolutions that may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Homomorphisms between Weyl modules for $\mathrm{GL}_3$ in characteristic $2$
papers.abstract: We classify the homomorphism spaces between Weyl modules for the general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_3$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $2$. We prove that these spaces have dimension at most one and give an explicit recursive procedure that determines when they are nonzero and constructs generators in terms of semistandard tableaux. As a consequence, we determine the dimensions of certain homomorphism spaces between Specht modules in characteristic $2$.

papers.title: Homotopy $n$-types of cubical sets and graphs
papers.abstract: We give a new construction of the model structure on the category of simplicial sets for homotopy $n$-types, originally due to Elvira-Donazar and Hernandez-Paricio, using a right transfer along the coskeleton functor. We observe that an analogous model structure can be constructed on the category of cubical sets, and use it to equip the category of (simple) graphs with a fibration category structure whose weak equivalences are discrete $n$-equivalences.

papers.title: Horrocks-Mumford sheaves on toric varieties
papers.abstract: Previous work of the authors introduced the class of Horrocks-Mumford sheaves over normal algebraic k-varieties, the most prominent example being the classical Horrocks-Mumford bundle on projective four-space. For a smooth semiprojective toric variety, we derive an explicit description of these sheaves in terms of finitely generated graded modules over the Cox ring which we use for an algorithmic treatment. In particular, we discuss some explicit examples, their indecomposability and local freeness.

papers.title: Ice and mirrors
papers.abstract:
Given a mirror pair of smooth affine principal upper cluster varieties admitting reddening sequences, we show that homological mirror symmetry for principal cluster varieties -- assumed compatible with certain cluster structures -- descends under freezing.
  This allows us to induct on the following class. A skew-symmetrizable matrix is peelable if, by mutations and removing sinks or sources, it can be reduced to the empty matrix; it is sub-peelable if it is a principal submatrix of a peelable matrix. We establish homological mirror symmetry for full rank upper cluster varieties whose mutable matrix is sub-peelable.
  We show sub-peelability for the Fock--Goncharov SL(n) quiver for any compact surface with nonempty boundary, all of whose boundaries have markings. Consequently, we establish homological mirror symmetry between the moduli of decorated SL(n) local systems and the corresponding pinned PGL(n) spaces. The results were obtained using ChatGPT Astra.

papers.title: Improving Razmyslov's (1974) bound: the Nagata–Higman index is at most n² − 2 for n ≥ 3
papers.abstract: Let $d(n)$ be the least $m$ such that every associative (not necessarily unital) algebra over a field of characteristic zero satisfying the identity $x^n=0$ also satisfies $x_1x_2\cdots x_m=0$; this is the Nagata–Higman index. Razmyslov proved $d(n)\le n^2$ in 1974; Kuzmin proved $d(n)\ge n(n+1)/2$ and conjectured equality; this is the Kuzmin (1975) conjecture. We prove $d(n)\le n^2-2$ for $n\ge3$ (and, by a simpler case of the same method, $d(n)\le n^2-1$ for $n\ge2$); in particular $d(6)\le34$. To our knowledge, $n=6$ is the first case in which the new bound improves the known bounds, and this is the first improvement of Razmyslov's bound for general $n$. For $m=n^2-1$ and $m=n^2-2$, Formanek's criterion reduces $d(n)\le m$ to the statement that no nonzero linear combination of $(m+1)$-cycles lies in one particular isotypic block of the group algebra of $S_{m+1}$. For $m=n^2-1$ this statement follows from the branching rule; for $m=n^2-2$ we prove it using the Jucys–Murphy elements and a theorem of Frobenius on the characters of the alternating group. These bounds have also been proved in the Lean proof assistant.

papers.title: Improving Razmyslov's (1974) bound: the Nagata–Higman index is at most n² − 2 for n ≥ 3, and other miscellanea
papers.abstract: Let $d(n)$ be the least $m$ such that every associative algebra over a field of characteristic zero satisfying $x^n=0$ also satisfies $x_1x_2\cdots x_m=0$ (the Nagata–Higman index). Razmyslov proved $d(n)\le n^2$ in 1974, and the Kuzmin (1975) conjecture is $d(n)=n(n+1)/2$. We prove $d(n)\le n^2-1$ for $n\ge2$ and $d(n)\le n^2-2$ for $n\ge3$; in particular $d(6)\le34$. The proof uses Formanek's criterion in cycle form and studies, one isotypic block of $S_N$ at a time, the span of the $N$-cycles inside the block: a block with two corners meets this span exactly when its shape is a self-conjugate hook, and for every $k\ge2$ the block of $(k+1,2,1^{k-1})$, which has three corners, meets it too. The next step, $d(n)\le n^2-3$, reduces to one statement about the block of $(n^{n-2},n-1,n-2)$; for every $n\ge4$ we prove the part of it that concerns the constituents with at most two rows of length $3$, and for $n=5$ the whole statement (computer-assisted). Through the hook theorem the question becomes one about the polynomial identities of Kemer's superalgebras $M_{k,l}$ over the Grassmann algebra: lower bounds for their PI degrees give upper bounds for $d(n)$, and the lower half of the Samoilov (2010) conjecture on these PI degrees would give $d(n)<\frac89n^2$ for $n\ge3$.

papers.title: Infinite Euclidean Distance Discriminants
papers.abstract: We study infinite Euclidean distance discriminants of algebraic varieties, defined as the loci of data points whose fibers under the second projection from the Euclidean distance correspondence are positive-dimensional. In particular, these discriminants contain all data points with infinitely many critical points for the nearest-point problem. We present computer code that computes the infinite Euclidean distance discriminant, and use it to present numerous varieties with nonempty such discriminants. Moreover, we prove that for any data point, the fiber under the second projection is contained in a finite union of hyperspheres centered at that point. For curves, we include a complete characterization; their infinite Euclidean distance discriminants turn out to be affine linear spaces. Finally, we introduce and characterize skew-tube surfaces in three-dimensional space. By construction, these have a one-dimensional infinite Euclidean distance discriminant. We further demonstrate that many skew-tubes have significantly lower Euclidean distance degrees than generic surfaces of the same degree.

papers.title: Integer and modular flow reconfiguration: the moduli up to six, chords, and large moduli
papers.abstract: For a finite multigraph $G$ and an integer $k\ge2$, let $\mathcal M_k(G)$ be the graph on the nowhere-zero $\mathbb Z_k$-flows of $G$, and $\mathcal I_k(G)$ the graph on the integer flows $F$ of $G$ with $1\le|F(e)|\le k-1$ on every edge; a step adds a nonzero constant along one cycle. The Esperet–Hendrey–Lagoutte–Marseloo–Norin–Steiner (2025) lifting question asks for a proof that $\mathcal I_k(G)$ is connected whenever $\mathcal M_k(G)$ is connected; its authors write that they do not know how to prove this even for $k=4$. We prove it for $k=2,3,4,5,6$ and every graph, in a stronger form: reduction modulo $k$ induces a bijection between the components of $\mathcal I_k(G)$ and of $\mathcal M_k(G)$. We prove the same for every $k$ on the graphs in which every cycle with more than nine edges has a chord between two vertices that are not neighbors on the cycle. We also prove that $\mathcal I_k(G)$ is connected for every bridgeless multigraph $G$ and every $k\ge\operatorname{mc}(G)+2$, where $\operatorname{mc}(G)$ is the largest number of edges of a cut of $G$; and that scaling by $m$ carries the components of $\mathcal M_k(G)$ into components of $\mathcal I_{mk}(G)$. With a theorem of Esperet et al. on planar graphs, the first result settles the question for every planar graph and every $k$. The bijection of the components for $k\le6$ holds more generally for the integer and modular kernel vectors of every totally unimodular matrix, with the circuit vectors as steps, and in this generality it fails at every prime $p\ge7$, for the tensions of a graph on $2p$ vertices; this does not answer the question for the flows of graphs. For the six moduli $k=8,9,12,16,18,36$ we prove the bijection of the components for every graph also; this is a short deduction from a lemma on liftable steps of a companion paper. For the other $k\ge7$ this paper does not settle the question on arbitrary graphs.

papers.title: Intersection theory and Chern classes on normal varieties II
papers.abstract: We prove a uniform bound linear in the rank for the local correction terms in the Riemann--Roch formula for reflexive sheaves on normal surfaces over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. We also establish the usual tensor and symmetric-power formulas for second Chern characters and prove Wahl's asymptotic Riemann--Roch conjecture and its higher-rank generalization. These results yield second Chern classes of reflexive sheaves on arbitrary normal projective varieties, compatible with pullback by finite surjective morphisms. We characterize their discriminants as infima of normalized discriminants of compatible vector bundles on smooth alterations. As applications we prove Bogomolov's inequality, effective restriction and boundedness theorems on normal projective varieties, a Miyaoka-type inequality, and a Segre-class criterion for bigness of reflexive sheaves on normal surfaces.

papers.title: Isolated Singularities Not Resolved by Iterated Nash Blowups
papers.abstract: Castillo, Duarte, Leyton-\'Alvarez, and Liendo asked whether iterating ordinary Nash blowups in characteristic zero or normalized Nash blowups in arbitrary characteristic can fail to resolve isolated singularities arXiv:2511.17862. We answer this question affirmatively with two constructions of isolated singularities, one nonnormal and one normal, both giving counterexamples to normalized Nash iteration in every characteristic.

papers.title: K-theoretic construction of affine quantum Schur algebras and iquantum groups with unequal parameters
papers.abstract: We present an equivariant K-theoretic construction of affine quantum Schur algebras of type C with three parameters by taking advantage of Kato's exotic framework. This enables the derivation of an equivariant K-theoretic realization of affine iquantum groups of type AIII with three parameters. Additionally, in Appendix A, we provide an equivariant K-theoretic construction of affine quantum Schur algebras of types B/C/F/G with two parameters, following Antor's recent work on affine Hecke algebras with two parameters.

papers.title: Koszul duality for finite-dimensional Koszul algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\La$ be a finite-dimensional Koszul algebra with Koszul dual $\Ld$. Using the Koszul functors and the homological perturbation lemma, we describe the minimal projective resolution of every object of the bounded derived category of finite-dimensional graded $\La$-modules in terms of the cohomology of the corresponding complex of coperfect graded $\Ld$-modules. In particular, the linear part of the minimal graded projective resolution of a finite-dimensional graded $\La$-module is a direct sum of Koszul complexes of these cohomology modules. We deduce that $\La$ is absolutely Koszul if and only if $\Ld$ is graded left co-coherent, if and only if the category of coperfect graded $\Ld$-modules is abelian. As applications, we show that absolutely Koszul algebras of finite global linearity defect have finite graded finitistic dimension; we refine the graded and ungraded Koszul dualities and construct nonstandard $t$-structures on the bounded derived and singularity categories. Finally, we apply these results to finite-dimensional quadratic monomial algebras.

papers.title: Kronecker Coefficients and Simultaneous Conjugacy Classes
papers.abstract: A Kronecker coefficient is the multiplicity of an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ in a tensor product of irreducible representations. We define Kronecker Hecke algebras and use them as a tool to study Kronecker coefficients in finite groups. We show that the number of simultaneous conjugacy classes in a finite group $G$ is equal to the sum of squares of Kronecker coefficients, and the number of simultaneous conjugacy classes that are closed under elementwise inversion is the sum of Kronecker coefficients weighted by Frobenius-Schur indicators. We use these tools to investigate which finite groups have multiplicity-free tensor products. We introduce the class of doubly real groups, and show that they are precisely the real groups which have multiplicity-free tensor products. We show that non-Abelian groups of odd order, non-Abelian finite simple groups, and most finite general linear groups do not have multiplicity-free tensor products.

papers.title: Lifting the local logarithmic Cartier transform modulo $p^n$
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime number and $n\ge 1$ an integer. We construct a local logarithmic Cartier transform modulo $p^n$, following an approach by Shiho. More precisely, consider the ring $W$ of Witt vectors of a perfect field of characteristic $p$. Let $f:\mathfrak{X}\rightarrow \mathfrak{S}$ be a log smooth morphism of fs logarithmic $p$-adic formal schemes, whose underlying formal schemes are flat and locally of finite type over $W$, and assume the exact relative Frobenius after reduction modulo $p$ admits a lift $F$. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be Lorenzon's indexed algebra on the reduction modulo $p^n$ of $\mathfrak{X}.$ We define an indexed subalgebra $\mathcal{B}_F\subset\mathcal{A}$ and equip it with an integrable quasi-nilpotent $p$-connection. Our main result is an equivalence between the category of indexed $\mathcal{B}_F$-modules equipped with integrable quasi-nilpotent $p$-connections compatible with the $p$-connection on $\mathcal{B}_F$, and the category of indexed $\mathcal{A}$-modules equipped with integrable quasi-nilpotent connections compatible with the canonical connection on $\mathcal{A}$. This gives a local logarithmic version of the Cartier transform modulo $p^n$.

papers.title: Linear Algebra over Bands
papers.abstract: We introduce Eckmann-Hilton operators on bands, which allow for a suite of matroidal constructions, in particular, matroid unions and matroid stable intersections. This enables the construction of general linear monoids over bands. Geometrically, we show that matroid stable intersection extends the transverse intersection of linear spaces over fields and the stable intersection of tropical linear spaces, lending new insight into intersection theory on bands.

papers.title: Log Hodge-de Rham degeneration beyond the toroidal case
papers.abstract:
Let $\phi\colon X \to S$ be a flat and proper one-parameter degeneration of algebraic varieties with a single degenerate fiber $X_0$. If $\phi\colon (X|X_0) \to (S|0)$ is log smooth and saturated, the log Hodge-de Rham spectral sequence is known to degenerate at the page $E_1$. Adding to that some further well-known related properties, we say that the log de Rham complex $\Omega^{\bullet,\mathrm{log}}_{X/S}$ is cohomologically flat as a filtered complex, short cffc. Furthermore, if $\phi\colon (X|X_0) \to (S|0)$ has only toroidal log singularities, it is known that the reflexive log de Rham complex $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ is cffc. A major motivation to study this property is that in the Calabi-Yau case, $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ being cffc implies that a certain logarithmic deformation functor for $\phi_0\colon X_0^\partial \to S_0^\dagger$ is unobstructed.
  In this article, we develop a computational criterion to determine, under very mild assumptions on $\phi\colon X \to S$, whether the reflexive log de Rham complex $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ is cffc. Applying this criterion, we found many explicit examples of degenerations of surfaces where $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ is cffc, even though the log singularities are worse than toroidal. We did not find any new examples of degenerations of threefolds such that $\mathcal{W}^\bullet_{X/S}$ is cffc.

papers.title: Manin's conjecture for semi-integral curves and $\mathbb A^1$-connectedness
papers.abstract: We explore log Manin's conjecture for integral points and its connections to $\mathbb A^1$-connectedness. We prove log Manin's conjecture for Campana rational curves and for $\mathbb A^1$-curves on split toric varieties. Our arguments combine the Cox ring description of the moduli space of rational curves with Batyrev's heuristic-type counting arguments. As our proofs are geometric in nature, they give a geometric explanation of the mysterious leading constant for Campana points proposed by Chow--Loughran--Takloo-Bighash--Tanimoto.

papers.title: Maximality of the Do\v{s}en--Petri\'c Boolean Category
papers.abstract: We prove that the zero-identity Boolean category of Do\v{s}en and Petri\'c, freely generated by a nonempty set of propositional variables, is maximal. Adjoining any equation between parallel morphisms that does not follow from the defining equations, and closing under the operations on morphisms and uniform formula substitution, collapses this category to a preorder. This disproves their conjecture that the category is not maximal. The proof uses Boolean Coherence to select a pair of variable occurrences on which the two morphisms differ. Composition with morphisms selecting these occurrences, uniform substitution and two isomorphisms yield equality of the product projections. We prove that any zero-identity Boolean category satisfying such an additional equation under every interpretation of the variables is a preorder. We also give a Lean formalization of these proofs and their dependencies. It includes Boolean Coherence and the correspondence between substitution on tagged occurrence sets and substitution on finite ordinals.

papers.title: Maximum likelihood degrees of 3D polytopes built from polygons of ML degree one
papers.abstract: We construct 3D polytopes that admit a scaling with maximum likelihood (ML) degree one by using codimension zero toric fiber products of lower-dimensional polytopes and classify all the 3D polytopes that can be constructed in this way. We also study a family of 3D polytopes whose faces admit ML degree one scalings. We give a tight lower bound for the ML degree of these polytopes with a square base and we show that every value between this bound and the normalized volume of the polytope can be attained. These values depend on counting common and repeated roots associated to certain univariate polynomials. This is similar in spirit to the description of the possible ML degrees of rational normal scrolls.

papers.title: Modular Kittaneh Numerical Radius Inequalities
papers.abstract: We show that for adjointable morphisms on Hilbert C*-module over a commutative unital C*-algebra, a version of breakthrough numerical radius inequalities obtained by Kittaneh [\textit{{Stud. Math.}, 2005}] hold.

papers.title: Monodromy of rational singularities on surfaces in mixed characteristic
papers.abstract: We study the monodromy on the $\ell$-adic cohomology of smooth proper surfaces over complete discrete valuation fields of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, with algebraically closed residue field and $p>5$. When the surfaces admit proper models whose special fiber has at worst a rational double point, we show that the monodromy action of inertia is finite, depends on an \'etale neighborhood of the singularity and its nontrivial part coincides with a restriction of the reflection representation of a Weyl group naturally associated with the singularity. We extend this description for degenerations into general rational singularities whose deformations lie in the Artin component: the monodromy is described by restricting the reflection representation of the Weyl group associated with the exceptional $(-2)$-curves in the minimal resolution of the special fiber. Moreover we determine minimal finite extensions over which such surfaces have good reduction. The proof relies on a mixed-characteristic extension of Grothendieck--Springer simultaneous resolutions and an identification of monodromy and Springer representations via relatively perverse nearby cycles.

papers.title: N\'eron Functions on Jacobians of Odd-Degree Hyperelliptic Curves
papers.abstract: We express N\'eron functions on Jacobians of odd-degree hyperelliptic curves of arbitrary genus in terms of admissible pairings, using the pullback of the theta divisor via a generalized Abel--Jacobi morphism. Over non-archimedean local fields, we relate N\'eron functions to local N\'eron pairings on the curve and, moreover, deduce a comparison between unramified $p$-adic N\'eron functions and unramified local Coleman--Gross height functions. Furthermore, we decompose the N\'eron function into an intersection term $I$ and a Green function term $T$, and compute $T$ for specific semistable reduction types. We compare our decomposition with other decompositions in the literature.

papers.title: Nazarov-Sklyanin Lax operators at higher rank
papers.abstract: We construct a rank-$m$ Nazarov-Sklyanin Lax operator for generalized Macdonald functions. The operator acts on the horizontal Fock module of quantum toroidal $\mathfrak{gl}_1$, extended by an auxiliary polynomial space with $m$ components. A geometric realization is given by the tensor product with the dual tautological line on the equivariant $K$-theory of a Hecke correspondence studied by Negut. The eigenbasis is indexed by an $m$-tuple of partitions and an addable corner, whose content is the eigenvalue. We give an anti-normal factorization and prove that the Lax operator is self-adjoint for the transported Euler pairing. With unit framing weight, the rank-one specialization recovers the Nazarov-Sklyanin factorization. We then show that the Lax operator is conjugate to the companion matrix of a projected q-Miura operator of the deformed $W$-algebra of type $\mathfrak{gl}_m$. This also gives an explicit presentation of the $K$-theory of the Hecke correspondence.

papers.title: Non-algebraicity of non-abundant foliations and abundance for adjoint foliated structures
papers.abstract:
Assuming the abundance conjecture in dimension $d$, we establish a non-algebraicity criterion of foliations: any log canonical foliation of rank $\le d$ with $\nu\neq\kappa$ is not algebraically integrable, answering question of Ambro--Cascini--Shokurov--Spicer. Under the same hypothesis, we prove abundance for klt algebraically integrable adjoint foliated structures of dimension $\le d$ and show the existence of good minimal models or Mori fiber spaces. In particular, when $d=3$, all these results hold unconditionally.
  Using similar arguments, we solve a problem proposed by Lu and Wu on abundance of surface adjoint foliated structures that are not necessarily algebraically integrable.

papers.title: Non-factorisable Yangian Lax matrices through oscillators
papers.abstract: We construct oscillator realisations of Yangian Lax operators in type $A$, with particular interest in non-factorisable operators associated with prime snake modules. Our construction applies to finite-dimensional skew representations of $Y(\mathfrak{gl}_n)$. We prove that these representations are generated by the tensor vacuum in suitably ordered tensor products of oscillator representations. Their Lax operators are obtained by restricting the corresponding products of linear oscillator Lax operators to these submodules. We determine the vacuum eigenvalues and Drinfeld polynomials, and give a determinant formula for the dimensions directly in terms of the highest loop weights. A $21$-dimensional example illustrates the construction, including an explicit basis and a transfer-matrix identity.

papers.title: Non-tempered GGP conjecture for classical groups: the Bessel case
papers.abstract: In their recent paper, Gan, Gross and Prasad proposed a precise conjecture to describe the restrictions of representations of classical groups that lie in an L-packet of Arthur type. On top of local root numbers, the main notion considered is the relevance of two A-parameters. In this paper, we establish that the relevance of two A-parameters is sufficient for the existence of a Bessel period for a pair of representations in the associated L-packets. Moreover, such a pair is unique. We also prove the necessity of relevance for co-tempered A-parameters, and give several counterexamples in the general case.

papers.title: Nontrivial Massey products on compact K\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that the bigraded quasi-isomorphism type of the bigraded, bidifferential algebra of forms on a compact K\"ahler manifold generally contains more information than the de Rham cohomology algebra with its real Hodge structure. More precisely, on any closed Riemann surface of genus at least two, there is a nontrivial ABC-Massey product. Furthermore, starting from dimension three, there are simply connected projective manifolds with a nonzero ABC-Massey product of three divisor classes. In particular, compact K\"ahler manifolds are generally not formal in the sense of pluripotential homotopy theory.

papers.title: Nowhere-zero flow reconfiguration in every finite abelian group of order at least 3024
papers.abstract: For a finite multigraph $G$ and a finite abelian group $\Gamma$, let $F(G,\Gamma)$ be the graph on the nowhere-zero $\Gamma$-flows of $G$ in which two flows are adjacent if the support of their difference is a cycle. We prove that $F(G,\Gamma)$ is connected for every finite bridgeless multigraph $G$ and every finite abelian group $\Gamma$ of order at least $3024$. The previous bound for all finite abelian groups, due to Esperet, Hendrey, Lagoutte, Marseloo, Norin and Steiner, is a number with $694$ digits; for the cyclic groups of prime order $p$ their bound is $p>2.26\cdot 10^{15}$. A theorem of an earlier paper of the author covers every group that is not cyclic of prime-power order and whose order has a divisor $d$ with $4\le d\le|\Gamma|/10$; from the order $100$ on, it leaves only the cyclic groups whose order is a prime power, twice a prime or three times a prime. For a cyclic factor $\mathbb{Z}_n$ we use units of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ as scales, and we average over a set of scales that is generated by good units. Counts of the bad units settle the orders from $3999$ on, and a finite arithmetic certificate with $230$ rows settles the orders from $3024$ to $3998$.

papers.title: Odd-degree cycles and rationality of Peskine sixfolds of discriminant 24
papers.abstract: Benedetti and Faenzi conjectured that, for a general trivector $\sigma\in\mathcal D^{1,6,10}$, the Peskine sixfold $X_1^\sigma$ is rational if the Brauer class $\beta$ on the associated K3 surface vanishes. We prove this implication for every $\sigma$ in a nonempty Zariski open subset $U\subset\mathcal D^{1,6,10}$. When $\beta=0$, we construct a line on the generic fiber of the Peskine fibration after a cubic field extension and use odd-degree descent to obtain a line over the original function field. We extend criteria for rationality to smooth complete intersections of an arbitrary number of quadrics under suitable hypotheses. Finally, we describe the derived category of the generic fiber of the Peskine fibration in terms of a twisted nodal curve of arithmetic genus two.

papers.title: On $\iota$Quiver (BPS) Algebras and (Strict) Partitions
papers.abstract: We consider the $\iota$quiver algebras of split type associated with the quiver BPS algebras of affine type A. They are supposed to give twisted affine Yangians and (elliptic) $\iota$quantum toroidal algebras that could possibly arise from D-branes on $\mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{Z}_n$ with orientifolds. We mention some properties of these algebras, such as the minimalistic presentations in the rational cases and the coideal structures. We also investigate how one might identify these algebras from the quiver theories with orientifold actions. Moreover, we discuss some representations with combinatorial bases of these algebras. In particular, the algebras with $n=1,2$ in certain limits of the parameters have representations labelled by (coloured) strict/symmetric partitions, which in the case of $n=1$ recovers the known BPS counting of certain theories.

papers.title: On Milnor and Tjurina numbers of Pairs of Holomorphic Function Germs
papers.abstract: Motivated by the bifurcation formula for the Milnor number of pairs of holomorphic function germs, we introduce, via foliation theory, the Tjurina number of such pairs. We define it as the generic value of the Tjurina number of the foliation associated with the pair, with respect to a specified family of balanced divisors of separatrices. We prove that this value is well defined and that it is an analytic invariant, we derive an explicit formula for it, and we establish a bifurcation formula. As an application, we characterize semitame pairs in terms of this invariant. We also prove a version of Teissier's lemma for pairs and an upper bound for the Milnor number of a pair, and we apply these results to generic pencils of algebraic curves.

papers.title: On Pseudo-Effectivity and Volumes of Adjoint Classes in K\"ahler Families with Projective Central Fiber
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to studying the deformation behavior of pseudo-effective canonical divisors and volumes of adjoint classes in K\"ahler families. Based on recent developments in the K\"ahler minimal model program, for flat families with fiberwise canonical singularities, we establish the global stability of the pseudo-effectivity of canonical divisors and uniruledness, assuming in addition that one fiber is projective, while the same conclusion for K\"ahler threefolds is also true without the projectivity assumption of the central fiber. For a smooth K\"ahler family whose central fiber is projective with a big adjoint class, we show that its volume remains locally constant. Finally, using the (relative) minimal model program for K\"ahler threefolds, we verify the deformation invariance of volumes of adjoint classes and plurigenera for smooth K\"ahler families of threefolds, thereby partially confirming Siu's invariance of plurigenera conjecture in dimension three.

papers.title: On the continuity of the geometric side of the twisted trace formula
papers.abstract: We establish the continuous extension of the geometric side of the twisted trace formula to a natural space of test functions, which are not necessarily compactly supported, for reductive algebraic groups. The continuity of the geometric side of the (untwisted) Arthur trace formula was established by Finis--Lapid. Subsequently, Parab generalized their result to the twisted trace formula under a certain restriction on the truncation parameter and an additional assumption. In this paper, we remove his restriction and assumption, and prove the continuous extension for the twisted trace formula. We also give a revised form of Parab's decay estimate for the geometric side.

papers.title: On the effective Yau--Tian--Donaldson conjecture for projective bundles
papers.abstract: Consider the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(E)$ of a holomorphic vector bundle $E$ over a smooth curve, equipped with a fixed K\"ahler class $[\omega]$. Our first main result establishes that the existence of an extremal K\"ahler metric in $[\omega]$ is equivalent to the weighted stability of a moment polytope $\Delta$ with respect to explicit weight functions depending on the topological data of $\mathbb{P}(E)$. We then introduce a class of test configurations, which we call compatible test configurations. These are constructed by gluing horospherical test configurations of the fibers, arising from convex functions on $\Delta$ via Delcroix's construction, to the principal bundle associated with $\mathbb{P}(E)$. Our second main result shows that the weighted stability of $\Delta$ naturally arises when computing the relative uniform K-stability of $[\omega]$ with respect to compatible test configurations.

papers.title: On the internal homotopy theory of the motivic homotopy category
papers.abstract:
We develop an $\infty$-categorical framework for internal homotopy theory (truncations, homotopy groups, and Eilenberg-MacLane objects) of an accessible localization of an $\infty$-topos. For the motivic localization over a perfect field $k$, we show that a motivic space has trivial motivic $n$-truncation iff it has trivial Nisnevich $n$-truncation ($n\geq-2$), identifying internal $n$-Eilenberg-MacLane objects with strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant sheaves of groups when $n=1$ and strictly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant sheaves of abelian groups when $n\geq2$. We further prove that a generically free Nisnevich group sheaf is strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant iff it is birational (which for the free group sheaf $L_{nis}F_{grp}A$ holds iff $A$ is birational), whereas for an \'etale-weakly unramified sheaf of sets $A$, $L_{nis}F_{grp}A$ is $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant iff $A$ is itself $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant. Non-birational, \'etale-weakly unramified motivic sheaves of sets (such as $\mathbb{G}_m$) thus generate (non-abelian) $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant group sheaves that are not strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant. Combining this obstruction with essentially smooth base change, we prove that for a qcqs scheme $S$, $\mathcal{H}^{mot}(S)$ is an $\infty$-topos iff $S=\emptyset$.
  We also study relative truncation and connectivity under a localization. Over a qcqs scheme $S$, this identifies external $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-coverings with internal motivic $n$-coverings via pullback along the localization unit, yielding a motivic $n$-Galois correspondence over $k$. For connective morphisms over $k$, we establish a higher $\mathbb{A}^1$-Van Kampen theorem and a Nisnevich-local-to-global $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-connectivity criterion; in particular, a $k$-scheme is $\mathbb{A}^1$-connected iff it admits a Nisnevich cover by $\mathbb{A}^1$-connected schemes whose pairwise fiber products have $k$-points.

papers.title: On the Iterates of Endomorphisms of Projective Varieties
papers.abstract: We initiate a study of certain notions related to the algebraic dynamics of endomorphisms of projective varieties. Our main results include: (i) a characterization of projective varieties that occur as iterated images of endomorphisms of normal projective varieties; (ii) exploring stability behavior in the Stein factorizations of the iterates; and (iii) a structure result concerning endomorphisms whose iterates lie in a finite union of connected components of the endomorphism scheme, thereby completing a result of Brion.

papers.title: On the Milnor classes of local complete intersections
papers.abstract: In this work we study algebraic, geometric and topological properties of the Milnor classes of local complete intersections with arbitrary singularities. We describe first the Milnor class of the intersection of a finite number of hypersurfaces, under certain conditions of transversality, in terms of the Milnor classes of the hypersurfaces. Using this description we obtain a Parusi\'{n}ski-Pragacz type formula, an Aluffi type formula and a description of the Milnor class of the local complete intersection in terms of the global L\^e cycles of the hypersurfaces that define it. We consider next the general case of a local complete intersection $Z(s)$ defined by a regular section $s$ of a rank $r$ holomorphic bundle $E$ over a compact manifold $M$, $r \geq 2$. We notice that $s$ determines a hypersurface $Z(\tilde s)$ in the total space of the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(E^{\vee})$ of the dual bundle $E^{\vee}$, and we give a formula expressing the total Milnor class of the local complete intersection $Z(s)$ in terms of the Milnor classes of the hypersurface $Z(\tilde s)$.

papers.title: On the Residue Sequence in Logarithmic Topological Cyclic Homology
papers.abstract: Algebraic K-theory participates in localization sequences, as first established by Quillen. We identify their boundary maps with the \emph{residue} map from logarithmic TC under the cyclotomic trace, resolving a conjecture of Rognes. As a consequence, we obtain e.g. a trace map from the K-theory of periodic complex K-theory to the logarithmic TC of connective complex K-theory. Moreover, we find that there exists a stable infinity-category C such that TC(C) realizes logarithmic TC for specific log structures, such as the natural ones on discrete valuation rings, connective complex K-theory, and truncated Brown--Peterson spectra. This provides evidence for the existence of a category of modules in the context of logarithmic geometry. We conjecture that such a category can be chosen to reflect additional structure on logarithmic TC, and we give evidence for this for discrete valuation rings.

papers.title: On the volume of amoebas of complete intersections
papers.abstract: We study the $2k$-dimensional volume of the amoeba of a smooth complete intersection $V$ of dimension $k$ in $(\C^*)^n$, $n\ge2k$, with Newton polytopes $\Delta_1,\dots,\Delta_{n-k}$. For $n=2k$ we prove $\Vol(\A(V))\ge\mathcal M(V)/\MV(\Delta_1,\dots,\Delta_k,-\Delta_1,\dots,-\Delta_k)$, where $\mathcal M(V)$ is the coamoeba volume counted with multiplicity, and we show $\mathcal M(V)\ge\pi^{2k}$ for plane curves ($k=1$, $n=2$) whose Newton polygon is not centrally symmetric, for nondegenerate varieties with odd $\MV(\Delta_1,\dots,\Delta_k,\Delta_1,\dots,\Delta_k)$, and for smooth towers of curve fibrations. We determine the equality case for curves and towers, and prove that $k$-planes in general position never attain the bound. For $n>2k$ we prove two-sided bounds for $\Hm^{2k}(\A(V))$ through coordinate projections, and show that for generic coefficients almost every fibre of the amoeba map is an orbit of a finite group. For lines we prove that in several random models the area of the amoeba of a line in $(\C^*)^n$ is asymptotic to $\frac\pi2n\log n$, and we compute its limit under degenerations of the configuration. Finally we characterise the varieties attaining the extremal volumes. For $n=2k$ every regular fibre of the amoeba map has an even number of points, divisible by $4$ for real varieties with $k\ge2$; the volume-maximal varieties are those with two-to-one amoeba maps and maximal rolled coamoebas, and they are never real when $k\ge2$; a volume-minimal plane curve is characterised by a group of symmetries of maximal order, and its amoeba has no holes. For $n>2k$ the extremal varieties lie in translates of $2k$-dimensional subtori.

papers.title: On two-dimensional affine Springer fibres
papers.abstract: We extend results of Spaltenstein on irreducible components of two-dimensional usual Springer fibres in reductive groups of simply lace type to the case of two-dimensional affine Springer fibres associated to loop groups. One of our methods is to relate these affine Springer fibres with certain subsets of the affine Weyl group.

papers.title: Orthogonal bases of symmetric unitary matrices in odd dimensions and the mixed-unitary rank of the symmetric Werner–Holevo channel
papers.abstract: Let Sym_n denote the space of complex symmetric n×n matrices with the Hilbert–Schmidt inner product. Girard, Leung, Levick, Li, Paulsen, Poon and Watrous showed that the symmetric Werner–Holevo channel on M_n has minimal mixed-unitary rank binom(n+1,2) if and only if Sym_n admits an orthogonal basis consisting of unitary matrices. They established this for even n and for n=3, and conjectured it for all odd n; Levick and Rahaman settled the case of primes n≡7 (mod 8). We introduce a family of symmetric unitaries (“chirped circulants”) for odd n and prove that, for this family, the pairwise orthogonality conditions reduce exactly to a square system of (n^2-1)/4 real equations in as many unknown phases. Using this reduction we give (i) a fully explicit basis for n=5, with all entries in an explicit degree-8 number field and an exact-arithmetic verification, and (ii) a computer-assisted proof, based on the Krawczyk operator evaluated in Arb ball arithmetic, that a symmetric unitary orthogonal basis exists for every odd n with 3≤n≤67. Consequently the conjecture of Girard et al. holds for all n≤68. We also record several obstructions to natural approaches for general odd n, and a further reduction for prime n.

papers.title: P = W conjectures for varieties with nilpotent fundamental group
papers.abstract: We prove the cohomological and the geometric $P=W$ conjectures for the moduli spaces of $G$-Higgs bundles and $G$-local systems on any smooth complex projective variety $X$ with nilpotent fundamental group, and any connected complex reductive group $G$. To the best of our knowledge, our results provide the first instances of $P=W$ conjectures beyond curves and abelian varieties. Finally, we provide examples of our theorem for classical groups: as a byproduct of this analysis we investigate when symplectic resolutions of the corresponding character varieties exist.

papers.title: Phase Transition and Spontaneous Translation Symmetry Breaking in Negative Temperature Point Vortex Ensembles
papers.abstract: We establish a canonical phase transition and spontaneous translation symmetry breaking for balanced two-species point vortices on the square torus. A sharp inequality identifies the transition at $\beta=4\pi^2$, below collapse at $\beta=16\pi$. In the intervening regime, all global minimizers form one translation orbit of an explicit dipole. We prove a large deviation principle below collapse and identify the uniform random phase, phase-centered Gaussian fluctuations, and precise partition asymptotics in the ordered regime. For general prescribed bounded strengths, we distinguish global ordering, local instability, and collapse.

papers.title: Polynomial twisted periods and affine vertex algebras
papers.abstract: We prove the conjecture of Kang, Lawrie, and Song that Zhu's $C_2$-algebra of a simply-laced boundary admissible affine vertex algebra is isomorphic to the Jacobian ring of an invariant potential obtained by lifting a polynomial twisted period from a Cartan subalgebra via the Chevalley isomorphism. We further identify the $C_2$-algebras of the corresponding Drinfeld-Sokolov reductions with the Jacobian rings of the restrictions of this potential to Slodowy slices. We also extend the Jacobian presentation to non-simply-laced principal boundary admissible affine vertex algebras, where the restriction of the potential to the Cartan subalgebra satisfies a Dunkl-singularity equation with root-length-dependent multiplicities.

papers.title: Powers of projective lines inside full flag varieties
papers.abstract: Up to now, symplectic foliations of Poisson varieties have been primarily studied from a set theoretic perspective by describing their symplectic leaves individually as orbit closures. In the direction of obtaining algebro-geometric characterizations, for the standard Poisson structure $\pi$ on the full flag variety $G/B_+$ of a complex semisimple algebraic group $G$, we prove that the irreducible components of the reduced part of the 0-degeneracy locus of $(G/B_+, \pi)$ are precisely the inclusion-maximal $T$-stable complete Poisson submanifolds of $(G/B_+, \pi)$ that are isomorphic to powers of $\mathbb{P}^1$. This characterization is based on a theorem that explicitly classifies the closed Richardson varieties of $G/B_+$ isomorphic to $(\mathbb{P}^1)^d$. In turn, this theorem is based on a general theorem for arbitrary $T$-stable subvarieties of full flag varieties $G/B_+$ isomorphic to $(\mathbb{P}^1)^d$.

papers.title: Presheaves and cocompletions in formal category theory
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between presheaf constructions and free cocompletions in the context of formal category theory, elucidating the coincidence between the two concepts in familiar settings. We show that, in a virtual equipment satisfying mild assumptions, free cocompletions under classes of weights are exhibited by presheaf constructions. We furthermore extend the theory of weighted colimits from enriched category theory to this setting, developing the concepts of atomicity and rank, and providing recognition theorems for presheaf objects, free cocompletions, and cocomplete objects. As an application of our methods, we construct free cocompletions, under arbitrary classes of colimit-small weights, of (possibly large) categories enriched in (not necessarily symmetric) monoidal categories and bicategories; this resolves a longstanding omission in the literature on enriched category theory. As a consequence, we obtain a categorified Eilenberg--Watts theorem, which extends the classical theorem for categories of modules for rings (seen as one-object Ab-enriched categories) to categories enriched in a bicategory.

papers.title: Projective Models of Genus 21 K3 Surfaces
papers.abstract: We construct projective models for general primitively polarized K3 surfaces $(S,h)$ of genus $21$ (degree $h^2=40$) inside the 12-dimensional fine quiver moduli space $X = N(3;3,4)$ parameterizing stable representations of the $3$-Kronecker quiver with dimension vector $(3,4)$. As a corollary, we show that the corresponding moduli space $\mathscr{M}_{21}$ is unirational and prove O'Grady's generalized Franchetta conjecture for genus $21$. Then we investigate the geometry of $(S,h)$ through its Fourier--Mukai partner $S' = M_{S}(4,h,5)$ and construct an explicit isomorphism $f : S^{[2]} \xrightarrow{\sim} S'^{[2]}$ together with a common closed embedding into the projectivization $\mathbb{P}^{17}$ of the space of global sections of the normalized universal bundle, using the polarization $H_2 - 4\delta_2$. Finally, we identify the Brill--Noether locus $\mathfrak{B} = \{Z \in S^{[3]} : h^0(F \otimes I_Z) \ge 2\}$ scheme-theoretically with the $\mathbb{P}^2$-bundle $Y' = \mathbb{P}_{S'}((F')^*)$ and exhibit an isomorphism $S^{[3]} \xrightarrow{\sim} M_{S'}(3,h',6)$.

papers.title: Quantale-Enriched Co-Design: Toward a Framework for Quantitative Heterogeneous System Design
papers.abstract: Monotone co-design enables compositional engineering design by modeling components as feasibility relations between required resources and provided functionalities. However, its boolean formulation cannot natively represent quantitative criteria such as cost, confidence, or implementation choice. In practice, these considerations are introduced through ad-hoc scalarization or by augmenting the resource space, which obscures system structure and increases computational complexity. Therefore, we develop a quantale-enriched theory of co-design in which resources and functionalities are quantale-enriched categories and design problems are quantale-enriched profunctors, which lifts co-design from boolean feasibility to quantitative evaluation. Series, parallel, and feedback composition remain valid over any commutative quantale, and change-of-base maps between quantales yield heterogeneous composition, so that subsystems evaluated in different local semantics can be composed in a common framework. Numerical examples on a target-tracking system and a UAV delivery problem demonstrate this framework and show how it avoids the drawbacks of boolean-only formulations.

papers.title: Quantitative similarities for amenable algebras of two-by-two matrix-valued functions
papers.abstract: We study norm-closed subalgebras $A$ of $\mathrm{C}(X,\mathrm{M}_2)$ containing the scalar functions, where $X$ is a compact metrizable space. We characterize amenability of $A$ by semisimplicity of its fibres and a uniform bound on the norms of the elements $2p-\mathrm{I}_2$ associated with their primitive idempotents. This bound is the exact similarity constant in the faithful representation given by the direct sum of all evaluations. In particular, an amenable algebra of this form admits a similarity to a nuclear $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra with cost at most $\sqrt{2\operatorname{AM}(A)-1}$. The estimate is sharp already for a two-dimensional algebra in $\mathrm{M}_2$. The similarity is constructed from positive matrix-valued functions which are continuous away from the scalar fibres. Although these functions need not be continuous everywhere, the induced algebra isomorphism preserves continuous sections. We also prove the corresponding results for locally trivial bundles of $\mathrm{M}_2$-algebras, and give a noncommutative example for which no continuous matrix-valued similarity is available.

papers.title: Quantum Cohomology and irrationality of K\"uchle fourfolds
papers.abstract: We prove that very general K\"uchle fourfolds of types (c1), (c6), (b8), and (b11) are irrational. The key ingredients are a new rationality criterion, based on the theory of Hodge atoms due to Katzarkov--Kontsevich--Pantev--Yu and its integral extension by Gu\'er\'e, and a computation of the action of quantum multiplication on the vanishing cohomology of these fourfolds, which uses a version of the Quantum Lefschetz Hyperplane Principle. Quantum multiplication acts as a scalar on the vanishing cohomology, and we give an enumerative interpretation of this scalar.

papers.title: Quantum periods and threefold flips
papers.abstract:
We study regularized quantum periods under birational contractions involving threefold flips. Let $g:X \dashrightarrow X'$ be a birational map between Fano threefolds with terminal quotient singularities which contracts exactly one prime divisor $E$ and extracts no divisor. We prove that
  $$
  \lim_{r \rightarrow +\infty}\widehat{G}_{X,rE}(t) =\widehat{G}_{X'}(t).
  $$
  The proof uses logarithmically smooth degenerations and positive discrepancies on good resolutions. Compatibility with orbifold invariants is proved using successive quotient-point extractions and the two-component orbifold degeneration formula.
  We also define stationary descendant invariants of projective terminal Fano threefolds by good resolutions and prove compatibility with a given projective $\mathbb{Q}$-smoothing. The period comparison extends to projective $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial terminal Fano endpoints under the same hypothesis on the birational map. Its proof compares the endpoints on a common resolution.

papers.title: Relationship between generic Hecke algebra modules and $0$-Hecke algebra modules
papers.abstract: Let $H_{R,a}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ be the Hecke algebra over a principal ideal domain $R$ with parameter $a\in R$. The representation theories of $H_{\mathbb{C}(v^{1/2});v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ and $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ differ substantially and have largely been studied independently. In this paper, we relate the categories of finitely generated modules of these two algebras through specialization functors from the category of finitely generated $H_{\mathbb{C}[v^{1/2}];v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$-modules. We first investigate the fundamental properties of these functors concerning dimensions, essential surjectivity, and characters. We then construct $H_{\mathbb{C}[v^{1/2}];v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$-modules which, through these functors, provide connections between skew Specht modules of $H_{\mathbb{C}(v^{1/2});v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ and $0$-Hecke skew Specht modules of $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$, and between Kazhdan--Lusztig cell modules of $H_{\mathbb{C}(v^{1/2});v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ and dual plactic class modules of $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$. Both families of $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$-modules are closely related to regular Schur labeled skew shape posets. We further explore how specialization functors relate the Frobenius characteristic to the quasisymmetric characteristic and connects the branching rules for skew Specht modules with those for $0$-Hecke skew Specht modules. Finally, we use the established connection with Kazhdan--Lusztig cell modules to obtain a result on the classification of dual plactic class modules up to isomorphism.

papers.title: Relative involutions and inverses in monoidal dualities and slice constructions
papers.abstract: Our goal in this paper is to work towards developing a framework for characterizing dualities of weak categorical structures. It is often the case that duality involutions are characterized by relations which are more general than $f^2=1$. Moreover, it is also true that many dualities cannot be expressed using involutions alone. We develop a framework of relative involutions and relative inverses to express these dualities at least within categorical and bicategorical structures. In particular, we utilize this framework to express the dualities of virtual double categories and some important constructions on them. In the second part, we explore the problem of slicing and consider how dualities of monoidal structures interact with slice constructions. We end by providing a construction for both enriched slice model categories and enriched coslice model categories.

papers.title: Representability of Intertwining Operators for Weak Modules of Vertex Operator Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a vertex operator algebra. For every weak $V$-module $W$, we construct a weak $V \otimes V$-module $\mathcal{R}(W)$ representing the bifunctor $\mathcal{I}\binom{W}{-\;-}$ of intertwining operator spaces, in the sense that there exists a natural isomorphism \[ \mathcal{I}\binom{W}{-\;-} \cong \Hom_{V\otimes V} \ab\big(-\otimes -, \; \mathcal{R}(W)). \] As applications of this natural isomorphism, we first establish a Yoneda-type lemma for spaces of intertwining operators, and then identify the unique largest locally restricted submodule $\mathcal{R}_{\lr}(V^\prime)$ of $\mathcal{R}(V^\prime)$ with the coend of the bifunctor $-\otimes-^\prime$: \[ \mathcal{R}_{\lr}(V^\prime) \cong \int^{M} M \otimes M^\prime, \] where $M$ ranges over restricted $V$-modules. Finally, the connection between $\mathcal{R}(W^\prime)$ and the regular representation $\mathfrak{D}_{\xi}(W)$ constructed in \cite{Li02} is established, where $\xi \in \C^{\times}$. In particular, if $V$ is a $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra and $W$ is a restricted $V$-module, then $\mathcal{R}(W^\prime)$ is also a restricted $V \otimes V$-module and is canonically isomorphic to $\mathfrak{D}_{\xi}(W)$.

papers.title: Resolution of ladder representations
papers.abstract: Let $\pi$ be a ladder representation of $\mathbf{GL}_m(F)$, $F$ a non-Archimedean local field. We construct an exact sequence of costandard modules, indexed by a lower Bruhat interval of a symmetric group and graded by the length, whose Euler characteristic is the determinantal formula of Tadi\'c and Lapid--M\'inguez. This is an analogue of the dual Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand resolution. The proof is combinatorial, through Jacquet modules and the Bruhat order; we also interpret the coresolution as a Cousin complex on Zelevinsky's space, which extends it to the balanced representations of Lapid--M\'inguez.

papers.title: Rigidity for Families of Abelian Varieties over $\mathcal{M}_{g,n}$
papers.abstract: We provide a new proof of Farb's theorem on the global rigidity of the period map $\mathcal{M}_{g,n} \to \mathcal{A}_g$. We extend this classification to essentially include the period map for $\mathcal{M}_{2,n}$. We also provide a classification of holomorphic maps $\mathcal{M}_g \to \mathcal{A}_{h}$ for $h \leq 2g-1$. The only nonconstant maps in this range are given by taking the Jacobian of a curve and attaching a fixed Abelian variety. In addition to the group theory of the mapping class group, we make extensive use of the theory of variations of Hodge structures and the birational geometry on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_2$.

papers.title: Sheil-Small's (1974) covering problem has a positive answer, and other miscellanea
papers.abstract: T. Sheil-Small asked whether every self-inversive polynomial maps the unit disc onto a domain that contains a disc whose radius is the largest modulus of the polynomial's coefficients (Problem 4.24 in Hayman and Lingham's problem book). We show that the answer is yes. More generally, every non-constant polynomial whose coefficients have the same moduli when read in reverse order maps the unit disc onto a domain that contains an open disc of this radius. This class contains both the self-inversive polynomials, whose zeros are symmetric with respect to the unit circle, and the polynomials whose zeros, with multiplicity, are symmetric under taking reciprocals (the literal reading of the problem as printed), so the theorem answers the question under either reading. The radius cannot be increased. For a polynomial with all its zeros on the unit circle, the largest disc in the image has radius exactly half the maximum modulus of the polynomial on the circle. For these polynomials the question is therefore equivalent to asking whether every coefficient has modulus at most half this maximum. O'Hara and Rodriguez and, independently, Saff and Sheil-Small proved this in 1974 for every coefficient except the middle one, and Kristiansen proved the middle case in 1979. The new case is that of polynomials with zeros off the unit circle. We treat this case with the Schur–Cohn Hermitian form of the polynomial minus a value that it does not take in the disc. This expanded version adds a description by rays of the image of a self-inversive polynomial, two examples, and the trigonometric form of the middle case. The results of Sections 2–5 are also proved in Lean 4, with the coefficient bound taken as given.

papers.title: Simple abelian varieties with prescribed endomorphism ratio
papers.abstract:
Let $A$ be a simple abelian variety over an algebraically closed field, and set $m(A)=2\dim A/[\operatorname{End}^0(A):\mathbb Q]$. We prove that, for every prime $p$ and every positive rational number $\mu$, there exist simple abelian varieties of characteristic $p$ with endomorphism ratio $\mu$, both of $p$-rank zero and of positive $p$-rank. In particular, we answer a question of Oort in a stronger form.
  Our construction combines Honda-Tate theory with explicit deformations of $p$-divisible groups using Breuil windows. An explicit Frobenius matrix, realized in a window with quaternionic multiplication, gives two reduced generic slopes with coprime denominators. Their coprimality, together with specialization and constancy of dimension, determines the full geometric endomorphism algebra. Polarized Serre-Tate theory and Grothendieck algebraization lift these deformations to abelian schemes. A related construction with an additional etale factor yields the positive-$p$-rank result.

papers.title: Smooth isometric bending of a closed sphere
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth embedded sphere $\Sigma\subset\mathbb R^3$ together with a smooth one-parameter family of isometric embeddings of $\Sigma$ whose images are not all congruent. The family is periodic; an inner disk and a complementary cap stay fixed pointwise; and the area, the enclosed volume and the total mean curvature do not change. This gives a flexible closed surface in the smooth category. The mechanism is elementary. A disk whose metric is rotationally symmetric, but whose embedding is not, can be turned inside a fixed shell provided it is exactly planar near its rim. The whole difficulty is to produce such a disk. This reduces to a scalar equation of Monge–Ampère type on an annulus, the Darboux equation, for a height function which must be nonradial and yet constant to infinite order at both boundary circles. We solve this equation by a Nash–Moser argument around an infinitesimal bending of a radial profile. The profile is forced to change the sign of its curvature infinitely often near each boundary circle, so the linearized equation changes type on infinitely many circles accumulating at both ends. We build the profile from explicitly solvable one-dimensional models, describe its accumulating ends by an exact three-term recurrence, and invert the linearized operator on the whole annulus. Two modifications of the linearization, each proportional to an unsolved equation, keep the type-change circles and the characteristic return maps fixed during the iteration, so that all linearized operators act on one domain.

papers.title: Smooth Numbers in Arithmetic Progressions with Uniformity in the Residue Class
papers.abstract: We improve the level of distribution of smooth numbers in arithmetic progressions to $x^{5/8-\epsilon}$, with uniformity in the residue class. In particular, for every $\epsilon,A>0$ and integer $k\geq1$, there exist $\delta,C>0$ such that $$ \sum_{\substack{q\leq x^{5/8-\epsilon}\\(q,a_1a_2)=1}}\tau_k(q)\sup_{0\leq z\leq x} \Biggl|\Psi(z,y;a_1\overline{a_2},q) -\frac{1}{\phi(q)}\Psi_q(z;y)\Biggr| \ll_{\epsilon,A,k}\frac{\Psi(x;y)}{(\log x)^A}, $$ uniformly for $x\geq2$, $(\log x)^C\leq y\leq x^{1/C}$, and $a_1,a_2\in\Z\setminus\{0\}$ satisfying $$ |a_1|\leq x^{1+\delta},\qquad |a_2|\leq x^\delta,\qquad (a_1,a_2)=1. $$ Here $\Psi(z;y)$ counts the $y$-smooth integers up to $z$, $\Psi_q(z;y)$ counts those coprime to $q$, and $\Psi(z,y;a,q)$ counts those congruent to $a$ modulo $q$; $\tau_k$ is the $k$-fold divisor function. The proof combines dispersion with second and fourth spectral moments.

papers.title: Spectral action in Betti metaplectic Langlands
papers.abstract:
We construct the spectral action in the context of Betti metaplectic Langlands theory. More precisely, we prove that the category of twisted sheaves on $\text{Bun}_G$ with nilpotent singular support admits a canonical action by the symmetric monoidal category of quasicoherent sheaves on the moduli of twisted $H$-local systems, where $H$ is the metaplectic dual group. This confirms the Betti version of the conjecture of Gaitsgory--Lysenko, originally formulated in the de Rham setting under the name ``metaplectic vanishing conjecture".
  Given a symmetric monoidal category with suitable symmetry, we develop a categorical framework by introducing a notion of twisted factorization homology and studying its categorical action. We show that the category of quasicoherent sheaves on the moduli of twisted local systems can be realized as a twisted factorization homology. Using metaplectic factorizable Satake we further prove that the metaplectic Hecke action naturally fits into our categorical framework. Combining these results, we obtain the desired spectral action.

papers.title: Spherical functions of the quantum symmetric pair of type FII
papers.abstract: We prove Schl\"osser's conjecture relating quantum FII spherical functions to Askey--Wilson polynomials for equal left and right coideal parameters and determine the corresponding radial operator. An explicit transport formula gives the shifted restrictions for arbitrary nonzero parameters.

papers.title: Stability conditions on Lazarsfeld-Mukai bundles over abelian surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the stability of Lazarsfeld-Mukai bundles associated with smooth curves over abelian surfaces. When the general curve in $|L|$ have Clifford dimension one and maximal gonality, for $\rho \gg 0$ we show that every component of the relative Brill-Noether loci \(W^1_d(|L|)\) dominating the linear system parametrizes generically \(\mu_L\)-stable rank-two Lazarsfeld-Mukai bundles. We also apply Bayer-Li wall-crossing to higher-rank bundles: if \(\operatorname{NS}(S)=\mathbb Z\cdot L\), \(A\) is a globally generated complete linear series of degree \(d\) on a smooth curve \(C\in|L|\), \(h^0(C,A)=r+1\) with \(r>2\), and \(d\ne g-1\), then the associated bundle \(E_{C,A}\) is \(\mu_L\)-stable and \(L\)-Gieseker-stable. The corresponding object \(E_{C,A}^{\vee}[1]\) for \(d<g-1\), or \(E_{C,A}\) for \(d>g-1\), is stable in the adjacent chamber, as its reduction. These results connect dimension estimates for Brill-Noether loci with stability and wall-crossing on abelian surfaces.

papers.title: Stability manifolds and resolutions of singularities
papers.abstract:
In this article, we study descent and lifting of Bridgeland stability conditions along Verdier quotients. We give a torsion-pair criterion for lifting every stability condition on the quotient to a weak stability condition with a prescribed heart on the null category. When this criterion holds for every heart on the null category, the space of weak stability conditions with this massless subcategory is homeomorphic to the product of the stability space of the quotient and the discrete set of hearts of bounded $t$-structures on the null category.
  We apply these results to contractions of relative dimension one, resolutions of nodal varieties, and blowups of smooth projective varieties along smooth centers. For projective surfaces with ADE singularities, we identify the discrete factor through a simply transitive braid group action. When the minimal resolution is a K3 surface, every weak stability condition obtained by lifting a numerical stability condition from the singular surface is the limit of a continuous, quasi-convergent family of numerical Bridgeland stability conditions on the resolution with the same heart.

papers.title: Stability of the tangent bundle on del Pezzo surfaces
papers.abstract: In this article, we study the Bridgeland stability of the tangent bundle on del Pezzo surfaces. We obtain a complete description of the region where the tangent bundle is (un)stable with respect to the standard Bridgeland stability conditions associated to the anticanonical polarization.

papers.title: Stabilizing Parabolic Vector Bundles
papers.abstract: For an irreducible parabolic flat vector bundle of rank $r < 2\sqrt{g}$ on a genus $g$ curve, we prove that an analytically general isomonodromic deformation is stable. This refines Landesman-Litt's semistability result for bundles of rank $< 2\sqrt{g+1}$. The proof applies the non-generically globally generated (non-GGG) lemma to establish infinitesimal obstructions to extending destabilizing subbundles of semistable bundles.

papers.title: Submatrices of character tables and centers of ordinary and queer q-Schur superalgebras
papers.abstract: We obtain bases of the centers of the ordinary $q$-Schur superalgebra $\mathcal{S}_q(m|n,r)$ and the queer $q$-Schur superalgebra $\mathcal{Q}_q(n,r)$ in terms of Casimir elements of the Hecke algebra $\mathcal{H}_r$ and the Hecke-Clifford algebra $\mathcal{H}_r^c$, respectively. The key step is to find an invertible submatrix of the character table of $\mathcal{H}_r$ or $\mathcal{H}_r^c$ whose column index set is the support of the corresponding $q$-tensor module appearing in Schur-Weyl duality: for $\mathcal{H}_r$ this is the set $H_{m,n}(r)$ of $(m|n)$-hook partitions of $r$, while for $\mathcal{H}_r^c$ this is the set $\mathrm{SP}_n(r)$ of strict partitions of $r$ of length $\leq n$. Unlike the case of ordinary $q$-Schur algebras, the submatrix formed by taking the row index set to be the same as the column index set need not be invertible. We determine that the row index set should be chosen as $H_{\min\{m,n\},\max\{m,n\}}(r)$ for $\mathcal{S}_q(m|n,r)$, and as the preimage of $\mathrm{SP}_n(r)$ under the Glaisher correspondence for $\mathcal{Q}_q(n,r)$.

papers.title: Symmetric Chemical Reaction Networks: Realizations and Steady States
papers.abstract: We investigate symmetric chemical reaction networks and their steady states. From classical equivariant dynamical systems and network theory it is known that the mass- action ODE of any symmetric chemical reaction network is equivariant. For symmetries that permute the species, we prove that any equivariant mass-action ODE is realized by a symmetric chemical reaction network and construct a sparsest such realization. We apply the half-degree principle to show that a symmetric CRN that has a steady state also has one with few distinct coordinates.

papers.title: The $E_6$-Grassmannian, its minuscule Coxeter matroids, and the lines on a cubic surface
papers.abstract: We study the minuscule Coxeter matroids of type $E_6$, whose ground set is the set of 27 lines on a smooth cubic surface. We characterize them by a tritangent exchange property and classify them into 230 orbits under the Weyl group. Every nonempty matroidal stratum of the $E_6$-Grassmannian is an open subscheme of a torus, and all orbits but one are realizable over every infinite field. Finally, we compute the tropical $E_6$-Grassmannian and its 60 classes of toric degenerations. This is an extended abstract for a forthcoming paper.

papers.title: The $k$-th Milnor and Tjurina numbers: conjectures and a bifurcation formula for pairs
papers.abstract: We study the higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated hypersurface singularities and extend these invariants to pairs of plane holomorphic germs. We first show that a conjectured upper bound of Hussain, Yau and Zuo on the ratio between the higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated hypersurface singularities in three-dimensional complex space does not hold: it fails already for the simplest singularity, a non-degenerate quadratic one, and the ratio tends to infinity as the order grows. We then prove that a conjecture of Shi, Yau and Zuo on semiquasihomogeneous singularities holds for plane curves, for every order and over formal power series, and show that it fails in dimension three. Using the theory of higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of foliations in dimension two, we introduce these invariants for pairs of plane germs. For every order, we show that the higher-order Milnor number of a pair is determined by the Milnor number of the pair and the algebraic multiplicity of the associated foliation, and we compute the difference between the higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of the pair. Finally, we establish a bifurcation formula comparing the higher-order Milnor number of a pair with that of the product of the germs. As a consequence, we characterize semitame meromorphic germs as those for which these two numbers agree at some order, or equivalently at every order.

papers.title: The Auslander--Reiten Conjecture for Igusa--Todorov Algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that every Igusa--Todorov Artin algebra satisfies the Auslander--Reiten conjecture. More precisely, let $V$ be an $n$-Igusa--Todorov witness, and let $t$ be the number of isomorphism classes of nonprojective indecomposable summands of $V$. If a finitely generated module $M$ satisfies $\Ext_A^i(M,A)=0$ for every $i>0$ and $\Ext_A^q(M,M)=0$ for $1\leq q\leq 2t+1$, then $M$ is projective. As applications, algebras of representation dimension at most three and algebras satisfying $J^{2m+1}=0$ for which $A/J^m$ has finite representation type satisfy the Auslander--Reiten conjecture.

papers.title: The Brauer-Manin obstruction on algebraic stacks
papers.abstract: For algebraic stacks over number fields, we define their Brauer-Manin sets, Brauer-Manin pairings, and extend the descent theory of Colliot-Th\'el\`ene and Sansuc. By extending Sansuc's exact sequence, we show the torsionness of Brauer groups of stacks that are locally quotients of varieties by linear groups. With mild assumptions, for stacks that are locally quotients or Deligne-Mumford, we show that the Brauer-Manin obstruction coincides with some other cohomological obstructions such as obstructions given by torsors under connected groups or abelian gerbes. For Brauer-Manin sets of these stacks, we show the properties such as descent along a torsor, product preservation are still correct. These results extend classical theories of those on varieties.

papers.title: The dual of separated metric compact Hausdorff spaces is an infinitary variety of algebras
papers.abstract: A metric compact Hausdorff space is a Lawvere metric space equipped with a compatible compact Hausdorff topology (which does not need to be the induced topology). These spaces maintain many important features of compact metric spaces, but the resulting category is much better behaved. We prove that the category of separated metric compact Hausdorff spaces is dually equivalent to a variety of infinitary algebras.

papers.title: The exact semisimplicity criterion for Brauer algebras of type $C$
papers.abstract: We determine exactly when the Brauer algebra of type $C$, denoted by $\B_r(C,\delta)$, is semisimple over $\C$, where $\delta\neq0$. We first analyze the two admissible cases for homomorphisms from the top layer to the second layer. We construct an auxiliary operator on the space spanned by symmetric Brauer diagrams with a fixed bottom partial diagram and exactly two horizontal edges in each row. Using this operator, we prove that, in each admissible case, the corresponding quadratic condition is necessary and sufficient for the existence of a nonzero homomorphism. The constant terms of these quadratic expressions depend on sums of contents of horizontal $2$-strips in bipartitions. We then show that a failure of semisimplicity is detected by cell modules in the second layer. Finally, by relating the content sums for admissible bipartition pairs to the known sums for horizontal $2$-strips in ordinary partitions, we obtain an explicit finite set of exceptional nonzero parameters.

papers.title: The G\"ottsche conjecture and the G\"ottsche--Yau--Zaslow formula
papers.abstract:
The aim of these notes is to give an account, intended for the non-specialist, of the two proofs of the G\"ottsche conjecture given, respectively, first by Tzeng, and shortly after by Kool, Shende and Thomas.
